description: Lokalna single-user aplikacja webowa do tworzenia i przechodzenia interaktywnych kursów. Architektura: Next.js (App Router) + TS + Tailwind + shadcn/ui. Persystencja plikowa: kursy w /courses/<slug>/ jako JSON, postęp w ~/.ai-lecturer/progress.json. Lekcje to statyczne artefakty (sekcje + widgety) generowane offline przez ralph loop przy użyciu skili init_course / generate_lesson — webapp tylko renderuje, edytuje, i zbiera spec do generacji. Widgety MVP: theory (markdown + KaTeX), quiz ABCD, code exercise z Pyodide i ukrytymi testami, demo Gauss filter, sandbox. Wizualnie wysoka wierność do specyfikacji w claude/design/ (tokens.css → CSS vars konsumowane przez Tailwind). LessonChat (AI tutor) i live agent log są poza MVP.

acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/lessonChat/context.ts exports buildPromptContext({ lesson, currentSectionId? }) → { systemPrompt: string, contextBlock: string }

systemPrompt template: 'You are an AI tutor for an interactive online course. Answer concisely (≤200 words unless code is needed). Stay focused on the lesson topic. If asked off-topic, redirect politely.'

contextBlock includes: lesson.title, lesson.eyebrow, lesson.description, lesson.estimatedMinutes; if currentSectionId given, append the active section's data serialized as text (theory.markdown for theory; question + options for quiz; taskMarkdown for code; etc.)
If currentSectionId not given, append a brief outline: titles of all sections in lesson with their type
Context capped at ~4000 chars total; if exceeded, truncate active section text first and append '… [truncated]'

POST /api/lesson-chat (US-053) wired through buildPromptContext: call with { lesson: <fetched from disk>, currentSectionId: req.body.sectionId }; pass result to connector as { systemPrompt, userMessage: '<contextBlock>\n\nUser question: <message>' }
LessonChat panel (US-052) tracks current scroll position → maps to nearest section heading via IntersectionObserver → sends sectionId in POST body
Vitest tests cover: context built with theory section, with quiz section, without section; truncation when content exceeds 4000 chars

Verify in browser using playwright-skill: scroll to a quiz section in seed lesson, ask 'What is this question testing?', confirm response references the quiz topic specifically (not generic lesson summary)
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
stories.notes: depends on US-052 + US-053

stories.title: LessonChat — streaming responses + Stop/cancel button
stories.description: As a user reading AI tutor responses, I want to see them stream token-by-token and have a Stop button to cancel mid-response, so long answers feel responsive and I can abort if the answer is going off-track.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/lesson-chat extended to support `Accept: text/event-stream` and respond with SSE stream of assistant tokens (one event per token chunk, with final 'done' event)
Agent SDK connector: use streaming API; subprocess connector: read stdout line-by-line and forward each line as SSE event; close stream on subprocess exit
LessonChat panel (US-052) calls SSE endpoint via EventSource for new messages; appends streamed tokens to assistant bubble in real time

Stop button (placeholder from US-052) becomes active during streaming; click → aborts EventSource on client AND sends DELETE /api/lesson-chat/<requestId> server-side which kills the subprocess / aborts SDK stream
On stop: assistant bubble keeps the partial text + appends italic '— stopped by user' suffix on its own line in --text-tertiary
Server tracks in-flight requests in a Map<requestId, AbortController | childProcess> so DELETE can resolve which to terminate
Auto-cleanup of finished requests from Map after stream end (avoid memory leak)
requestId generated server-side and returned in the first SSE event so client knows what to DELETE

Verify in browser using playwright-skill: send a question that requires a long answer, observe tokens streaming into the assistant bubble, click Stop mid-response, confirm bubble shows partial text + 'stopped by user' suffix, then send a new question and confirm it works
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
stories.notes: depends on US-053

stories.title: Author end-to-end QA test plan markdown (test-plan.md)
stories.description: As a maintainer of this app, I want a single markdown file describing how to manually verify all features end-to-end, including which test courses to generate and which user flows to walk through, so I can sanity-check a release in under an hour.
acceptanceCriteria: File written: test-plan.md at repo root

Document structure: Setup section (npm install, npm run dev, etc.) → 'Test Courses to Generate' (≥3 distinct topics chosen to exercise different widget mixes, e.g. one Short narrow topic, one Standard ML topic, one Comprehensive math/CV topic) → 'Walkthroughs' (numbered checklists per area)

Each test course entry includes: topic prompt to enter in Stage 1, refinement choices for Stage 2 (level + duration + theory/practice slider), expected approximate lesson count + module count, which widgets the course is expected to exercise

Walkthrough sections cover at minimum: dashboard (empty state + populated + Continue learning hero + search bar substring + slug-prefix), course creation wizard end-to-end (all 5 stages), lesson navigation (TOC, prev/next, mark complete, auto-advance, keyboard shortcuts j/k/⌘B/⌘., Reset session), each widget type (Theory, Quiz single + multi, Code with peek + stop, Demo, Sandbox, PlotImage, PythonPlot, ParametricExplorer, CodeCloze, DragMatch, DataTable, Video, Image, Histogram), LessonChat (open, ask question with section context, stop mid-stream, draft persistence), theme toggle persistence, sources panel (lesson-level + section-level), schemaVersion present in JSON, logo navigates home, user avatar dropdown

Each walkthrough item is a checkbox with explicit pass criterion (e.g. 'button morphs to Submitted ✓', 'card badge shows In progress · 1/N', 'PNG appears within 10s after first matplotlib install') — no vague 'works correctly'
Document references the relevant US-NNN for each section so failures can be traced back to the originating story
Document includes 'Known limitations' section listing things explicitly out of MVP (multi-user, IndexedDB, tutor without Claude CLI installed, etc.)
Document targets ≤30 minutes for an experienced reviewer to walk through, ≤60 for a new reviewer
Typecheck passes
stories.notes: Documentation-only — no code changes. Output: test-plan.md at repo root.

stories.description: As the course-generation backend, I want to iterate the lessons in course.json sequentially with one `claude -p` per lesson — no ralph.sh, no worktrees, no branches, no git push — so a single push hiccup or an overwritten dev backlog can never block course generation again. Reproduces the failure mode in courses/opencv-in-computer-vision-a-practical-intermediate-course/.generation.log (push exit !=0 on attempt 1 leaves orphan ref → all retries fail non-fast-forward → 0 lessons generated).
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/courses/generate no longer spawns ./scripts/ralph/ralph.sh; generation.ts is rewritten so after init_course it reads courses/<slug>/course.json and iterates lessons sequentially

For each lesson: spawn one `claude -p '...generate_lesson, slug=<slug>, lesson-slug=<lesson-slug>...' --dangerously-skip-permissions` in the main repo CWD; lesson JSON lands at courses/<slug>/lessons/<lesson-slug>.json and is validated against LessonSchema post-spawn
SSE stream still emits stage / log / progress / done / error events; progress emits current/total per lesson so the wizard's progress bar advances
A failing single lesson is recorded but does NOT abort the run; remaining lessons continue; the final done event includes a failedLessons summary (or an error event lists them if any failed)
Cancel (DELETE /api/courses/generate?id=...) terminates the in-flight lesson child cleanly (SIGTERM → SIGKILL grace, same as current)
After a full generation, `git diff` shows changes only under courses/<slug>/ — scripts/ralph/{prd.json,progress.txt,archive/} and .worktrees/ and any ralph/* branches stay untouched
generation.test.ts updated: GENERATION_MOCK=1 covers happy path (multi-lesson loop), single-lesson-failure isolation, and cancel mid-run; old ralph-spawn assertions removed
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

Also resolves the prd.json overwrite issue the user flagged separately, because scripts/ralph/ is no longer touched by this flow.

stories.title: Per-lesson retry + structured per-course log layout for course-generation pipeline
stories.description: As the new course-generation pipeline (US-097), I want each lesson's `claude -p` invocation to support up to N attempts with failure context fed back to the agent on retry, plus a structured log layout under courses/<slug>/.gen-logs/, so transient failures (rate limit, schema validation slip, timeout) don't kill a lesson and the audit trail of every attempt is preserved.
acceptanceCriteria: Per-lesson retry loop: configurable via env (LESSON_MAX_RETRIES, default 2 → 3 total attempts; LESSON_TIMEOUT_SEC, default 1800), retries on non-zero exit OR on LessonSchema validation failure of the produced JSON

On retry, the next `claude -p` prompt includes a 'PREVIOUS ATTEMPT FAILED:\n<reason>' block (reason: tail of stderr / Zod issues / 'exited with code N' / 'timeout after Ns') — mirrors ralph's pattern from scripts/ralph/ralph.sh:992-996
Per-attempt timeout: SIGTERM → wait sigkillGraceMs → SIGKILL (same pattern as the existing cancel handler in generation.ts:271-292); timed-out attempt counts as a failed attempt
Successful retry → lesson marked done, NOT included in failedLessons
Exhausted retries → lesson appears in failedLessons (SSE event payload + failed_report.json); pipeline continues with next lesson

Log layout per course: courses/<slug>/.generation.log (existing master tee, unchanged); courses/<slug>/.gen-logs/init_course.log (init stage output); courses/<slug>/.gen-logs/<lesson-slug>.log (all attempts appended, each preceded by '=== Attempt N — <ISO timestamp> ==='); courses/<slug>/.gen-logs/failed_report.json ([{lessonSlug, attempts, lastError, logPath}], only for exhausted-retry lessons)
.gen-logs/ committed to git (no .gitignore changes); matches existing pattern of .generation.log + ralph-logs/ in the opencv course folder

generation.test.ts covers: (a) first attempt fails → retry succeeds → lesson done, log has 2 attempt headers; (b) all attempts fail → lesson in failed_report.json, log has 3 attempt headers, pipeline still emits final done listing the failed lesson; (c) per-attempt timeout fires → SIGKILL grace → next attempt starts with PREVIOUS ATTEMPT FAILED context
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
stories.notes: Depends on US-097 (extends the new pipeline; nothing to extend if US-097 hasn't landed). Files: src/lib/server/generation.ts, src/lib/server/generation.test.ts, possibly add genLogsDir(slug) helper in src/lib/server/paths.ts.

stories.title: Add per-story 'timeout' field to ralph orchestrator (overrides TASK_TIMEOUT_SEC)
stories.description: As ralph orchestrator, I want each story in prd.json to optionally specify a `timeout` field (seconds) that overrides the global TASK_TIMEOUT_SEC for that single task, so long-running stories like end-to-end smoke tests can run autonomously without bumping the global timeout for everyone else.

stories.title: Fix: race in startGeneration lets concurrent POSTs spawn parallel pipelines
stories.description: As a user kicking off course generation, when two POST /api/courses/generate requests fire concurrently (e.g. React StrictMode double-mounting the Stage 5 effect in dev), both bypass the activeRun guard and start parallel pipelines. They share the same /courses/<slug>/ directory and overwrite each other's lesson files in /courses/<slug>/lessons/.
acceptanceCriteria: A failing test reproducing the bug exists before the fix (two concurrent startGeneration(slug) calls for the same slug)
The second concurrent call rejects with GenerationConflictError; only one pipeline runs
The activeRun guard check and assignment are atomic — no await between them
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
stories.notes: Repro: fire two POSTs to /api/courses/generate for the same slug in the same tick. Confirmed live during US-099 follow-up testing — a completed lesson JSON (architektura-opencv-i-ekosystem-pythona.json, 12.6 KB) was wiped by a parallel run's pre-attempt fs.unlink. Root cause: in src/lib/server/generation.ts startGeneration() checks activeRun synchronously but only assigns activeRun = run after several await fs.mkdir(...) calls — classic TOCTOU.

stories.title: Stream claude -p output incrementally during course generation
stories.description: As a user watching Stage 5 of /create, I want to see live progress while claude is generating so I do not think the app is hung. acceptanceCriteria: defaultInitCourseCommand and defaultLessonCommand in src/lib/server/generation.ts pass --output-format stream-json (and --verbose if required) to claude -p
pumpStream parses the stream-json events and emits human-readable per-event log lines (assistant text deltas, tool invocations) instead of a single end-of-stage blob
SSE log panel in /create Stage 5 shows incremental output while claude is still running
GENERATION_MOCK=1 test fast-path still works
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
stories.notes: User staring at "Waiting for output…" for tens of minutes is the symptom. Each stream-json event is one line of JSON on stdout — the existing pumpStream newline-splitter already handles that; the new code just needs to JSON-decode and pull out human-readable fields.

Truncated content ends with the literal marker `\n\n[…truncated, <N> more chars…]`. Files are read in lexicographic order; once the running total would exceed the budget, subsequent text files become `kind: 'text'` with `content` set to a single-line placeholder `'(omitted: total character budget exhausted)'` — they are NOT silently dropped, the user must see in the prompt that we know about the file.

loadStagedSourcesForPrompt returns [] for a missing draft directory (ENOENT), never throws. assertSafeDraftId is called before any filesystem access. Read errors on individual files (e.g. unreadable .extracted sibling) downgrade that entry to `{ kind: 'binary-unsupported' }` with originalName preserved and a server-console warning — they do not fail the whole call.

' (extracted from docx)' : ''} ===\n<content>` for text entries, or `=== <originalName> ===\n(binary file uploaded by learner; content extraction not yet supported — treat the filename as a hint about scope)` for binary-unsupported entries. The block is appended BEFORE the final 'Generate up to 10 clarification questions…' instruction line.

src/lib/wizard/structure.ts: StructureRequestSchema gains an optional `draftId: z.string().optional()` field. buildStructureUserMessage gains the same `sources?` parameter and appends the same `Learner-uploaded source materials:` block, BEFORE the final 'Generate the full module → lesson outline…' instruction line.

stories.title: docx extractor — strip base64 image data-URIs from mammoth markdown output
stories.description: As an agent reading a learner-uploaded .docx, the .extracted/<name>.docx.md sibling produced by US-124 today contains 95%+ garbage: mammoth.convertToMarkdown's default behavior embeds every image in the document as a `data:image/...;base64,…` URI inline in the markdown. Measured on the reference fixture `Lista pytań kierunkowych.docx`: total extracted markdown is 2,258,963 chars, of which 2,152,160 chars (9 base64 image blobs) are useless to the LLM — only 106,803 chars are actual prose. This wastes the wizard's char budget (US-125 caps at 30k = currently captures only 1.3% of real text), explodes generation prompts in init_course, and contributes nothing to comprehension since data-URI base64 is not vision-token content in a plain-text prompt.
acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/server/docx.ts: `extractDocxToMarkdown` passes a `convertImage` option to mammoth that replaces each `` with a literal `[image]` placeholder in the output stream — i.e. `mammoth.images.imgElement(() => ({ src: '' }))` followed by a markdown post-process that rewrites `![]()` to the literal string `[image]`, OR a direct `convertImage: mammoth.images.imgElement(() => ({}))` that emits an empty img which the post-process collapses. Final markdown MUST contain zero occurrences of the substring `data:image/` and zero occurrences of `;base64,`.

Choose ONE strategy for the placeholder and apply it consistently: a literal `[image]` token on its own line, with surrounding blank lines preserved so paragraph boundaries are not lost. Do NOT keep alt text (mammoth does not produce useful alt for embedded docx images — they are usually empty or noise).

The change is backward-compatible at the API surface: `extractDocxToMarkdown(srcPath, destPath)` keeps the same `{ ok: true, markdown, warnings } | { ok: false, reason }` shape; `markdown` is just smaller and free of base64.

Unit tests cover: extraction of a fixture .docx that contains at least one embedded image (e.g. assets/test-with-image.docx; either commit a small fixture or generate one in the test setup using `mammoth.extractRawText` round-trip) — assert the returned markdown contains `[image]` AT LEAST ONCE, contains the prose text from the document, and contains ZERO occurrences of `data:image/` or `;base64,` (use `expect(md).not.toMatch(/data:image\//)`); regression test: a docx with no images produces markdown with zero `[image]` placeholders and identical prose to the pre-fix behavior.

Smoke test (manual): re-upload `/home/nukeemann/projects/ai_lecturer/temp/Lista pytań kierunkowych.docx` (or the existing fixture in /mnt/c/Users/nukee/Downloads/) via the upload-sources endpoint into a fresh draft, then `wc -m <draft>/sources/.extracted/Lista pytań kierunkowych.docx.md` — assert the char count is BELOW 200,000 (was 2,258,963 pre-fix; expected ~107,000 post-fix); `grep -c 'data:image/' <sibling>` must return 0; `grep -c '\[image\]' <sibling>` must return ≥ 1.

Out of scope for this story: re-extracting docx siblings produced before this change (existing extracted .md files in courses/.drafts/ and courses/<slug>/.extracted/ stay as-is until the user re-uploads — their next upload triggers fresh extraction with the new code path); preserving image content as actual vision-content blocks (would require switching the entire prompt format from plain-text to multimodal — large architectural change, separate story); extracting to a different format (still markdown).
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
stories.notes: This is a one-function fix in src/lib/server/docx.ts plus a unit test. Discovered when measuring why the wizard's 30k char budget (US-125) captured only 1.3% of the reference docx — turned out 95% of the 'extracted' content was base64. After this lands, the same docx fits comfortably in even modest budgets, which unblocks US-128's budget bump.

stories.title: Wizard inline budget bump + verify on real PDF — full grounding pass through Clarify + Structure
stories.description: As a user uploading a real-world textbook PDF (the kind that runs ~80 pages of Polish prose, like the reference `Lista pytań kierunkowych.pdf`), US-125's wizard inlining today caps every source at 30,000 total chars across all files — enough for ~10–15k tokens. Bump the budget to 150,000 chars total and 60,000 per file (~55–60k tokens for Polish, fits comfortably in 200k Opus context with room for system prompt + draft spec + clarification answers + the model's reply), and verify end-to-end that the wizard's outline visibly tracks the contents of the PDF.

Out of scope: per-course or per-lesson text-scale overrides; affecting KaTeX rendered math (KaTeX produces inline SVG/HTML with its own font sizing — best-effort only, do not engineer a special path); affecting embedded `<iframe>` (Pyodide) content; predefined preset buttons next to the slider.

Wrapping every --fs-* in calc(... * var(--text-scale)) is a one-pass file edit; if a particular var resolves through another var, wrap whichever level holds the px literal so the multiply happens exactly once.

stories.title: Collections — file-based store + REST API + schema types
stories.description: As a developer, I want a backend-only foundation for course collections — a typed collections.json file under ~/.ai-lecturer/, a Zod schema, and CRUD REST endpoints — so the dashboard UI in the next story can attach to a stable contract. No UI yet; this story ships the storage and API only.
acceptanceCriteria: New schema file src/lib/schemas/collection.ts exports `CollectionSchema` (Zod): `{ id: z.string().min(1), name: z.string().min(1).max(80), courseSlugs: z.array(z.string().min(1)) }` and `CollectionsFileSchema = z.object({ collections: z.array(CollectionSchema) })`. Export inferred TS types `Collection` and `CollectionsFile`.

New module src/lib/server/collections.ts exports: `getCollectionsPath(): string` (returns `~/.ai-lecturer/collections.json` resolved via os.homedir()); `readCollections(): Promise<CollectionsFile>` — reads the file, parses+validates via CollectionsFileSchema, returns `{ collections: [] }` on ENOENT (file absent); `writeCollections(file: CollectionsFile): Promise<void>` — atomic write (write to `<path>.tmp` then rename) with `{ encoding: 'utf-8' }`, ensures `~/.ai-lecturer/` exists (mkdir recursive). Validate on read AND on write — a corrupt file returns `{ collections: [] }` after logging a single warning to stderr (do not throw to the API caller).

src/lib/server/collections.ts also exports helpers used by the API: `createCollection(name): Promise<Collection>` (generates id via crypto.randomUUID(), appends, persists), `renameCollection(id, name): Promise<Collection>` (404-style throw if missing), `deleteCollection(id): Promise<void>` (no-op if missing), `addCourseToCollection(id, courseSlug): Promise<Collection>` (idempotent — no duplicates in courseSlugs), `removeCourseFromCollection(id, courseSlug): Promise<Collection>` (idempotent). Course slugs are NOT validated against the courses directory — collections may reference unknown slugs (which the dashboard will simply skip rendering); this keeps the storage layer independent of /courses/ scanning.

New route src/app/api/collections/route.ts: `GET` returns `readCollections()` as JSON; `POST` accepts `{ name: string }`, calls createCollection, returns 201 with the new Collection. Both responses set `Cache-Control: no-store`.

New route src/app/api/collections/[id]/route.ts: `PATCH` accepts `{ name?: string }` and renames; `DELETE` deletes (always 204). `id` is path-validated against /^[A-Za-z0-9-]{8,}$/ — rejects with 400 on mismatch (defense against `..` or empty ids in URL).

New route src/app/api/collections/[id]/courses/route.ts: `POST` accepts `{ courseSlug: string }` and calls addCourseToCollection; `DELETE` accepts `{ courseSlug: string }` (in JSON body — Next.js DELETE supports body) and calls removeCourseFromCollection. Both return the updated Collection. courseSlug must match `/^[a-z0-9-]+$/` else 400.

Unit tests cover: read on missing file returns empty; read on a valid file parses; write+read roundtrip; createCollection appends and persists; renameCollection updates the named entry only; deleteCollection on missing id is a no-op; addCourseToCollection deduplicates; removeCourseFromCollection on absent slug is a no-op. Tests use a temp HOME (override via `process.env.HOME` in beforeEach + restore in afterEach) so they never touch the real ~/.ai-lecturer/.

Route tests cover: GET on empty store returns `{ collections: [] }`; POST creates and is reflected in next GET; PATCH renames; DELETE removes; POST /api/collections/<id>/courses adds a slug; DELETE /api/collections/<id>/courses removes it; bad id (`..`) → 400; bad slug (`Foo!`) → 400.

Out of scope: any UI work (US-133 owns it); migrating existing data (no prior collections.json exists); per-course ordering within a collection (insertion order is stable — that's enough for now); concurrent-write locking (single-user local app, the existing file-based persistence pattern in /courses/ does not lock either, see project memory `project_file_based_persistence.md`).
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
stories.notes: Storage location matches the established pattern: progress.json sits under ~/.ai-lecturer/ already (see memory). Collection IDs come from crypto.randomUUID() so the regex /^[A-Za-z0-9-]{8,}$/ is loose enough to fit a UUID and tight enough to reject path-traversal attempts. Deliberately no `ui` tag — pure backend; orchestrator will skip Playwright.

stories.title: Collections — dashboard grouping UI + create/rename/delete + move-to-collection + seed Widget Demos
stories.description: As a user on the dashboard, I want to organize my courses into named collections (e.g. an "IT" collection) and move any course there from the main list, with an automatic seed that places all the widget-demo courses into a single "Widget Demos" collection on first run so the dashboard isn't cluttered by demo material. acceptanceCriteria: src/app/page.tsx: alongside the existing `/api/courses` and `/api/progress` fetches in `loadData`, also fetch `GET /api/collections` and store its `collections: Collection[]` in component state. Re-fetch on the same focus event the existing loaders use.

src/app/page.tsx: replace the single `data-testid="course-grid"` block with a sequence of grouped sections: first an "Uncategorized" section (heading: `Bez kolekcji` — match the project's existing PL/EN mix in strings; if strings are split, follow whichever language the surrounding `My courses` heading uses, currently EN → use `Uncategorized`) listing every course whose slug is NOT referenced by any collection's courseSlugs, then one section per collection in the order returned by the API, each with the collection's name as heading and only the courses whose slugs are in that collection's courseSlugs (in the order they appear there). Each section reuses the EXISTING `course-grid` style block (`display: grid; gridTemplateColumns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(320px, 1fr))`). Empty sections (collection with zero matching slugs) are hidden. Each section has `data-testid="course-section"` and `data-collection-id="<id-or-uncategorized>"`.

Add a `+ New collection` button next to the `My courses` heading-row CTA (or directly under it on narrow viewports) with `data-testid="new-collection-cta"`. Click opens a small inline prompt (use a native `window.prompt` to keep scope tight — explicitly approved alternative would be a modal but not required here): on submit it POSTs to /api/collections, refetches collections, and the new (empty) collection appears as a new section heading.

Each collection section header has a small kebab/`…` button (`data-testid="collection-actions-<id>"`) opening a tiny menu with `Rename` (calls window.prompt → PATCH /api/collections/<id>) and `Delete` (window.confirm → DELETE /api/collections/<id>). Both refetch collections after success. Deleting a collection releases its courses back to Uncategorized; the API already does this implicitly because deletion drops the slug list.

Each course card gets a small `Move…` action (a button or kebab inside the card, `data-testid="course-card-move-<slug>"`) opening a popover listing `Uncategorized` + every collection by name; selecting one POSTs the slug to /api/collections/<targetId>/courses (and, if the source was a collection, DELETEs from /api/collections/<sourceId>/courses BEFORE the POST so a course is never in two collections at once); selecting `Uncategorized` only DELETEs from the source. Refetch collections after success. The popover closes on outside-click and Escape.

First-run seed: on dashboard mount, after the initial GET /api/collections, if the response is `{ collections: [] }` AND the courses list returned by /api/courses contains AT LEAST ONE of the demo slugs below, perform exactly ONE seed: POST /api/collections with `{ name: 'Widget Demos' }`, then for each demo slug PRESENT in the courses list call POST /api/collections/<newId>/courses. Demo slug list (hard-coded in src/app/page.tsx as a const Set): `['cloze-test','datatable-test','dragmatch-test','gauss-basics','histogram-test','image-test','pexp-test','plotimage-test','quiz-test','smoke-test','theory-test','video-test','widget-dev-guide']`. Real courses (opencv-w-wizji-komputerowej-od-podstaw-do-sar, opracowanie-pytan-na-obrone-licencjacka-zarzadzanie, pytorch-for-python-developers, sar-dla-inzyniera-ai-od-fizyki-radaru-do-produkcyjnego-atr-w-pytorch) are NEVER seeded. Subsequent dashboard loads see a non-empty collections file and skip the seed entirely — even if the user later deletes the Widget Demos collection, it does NOT come back (the empty-store check is the gate).

Search behavior: when the search input has a non-empty query, collapse all sections into a flat result grid (today's behavior) — section headings are hidden during search. When the search clears, the grouped layout returns. The existing `enriched` filter logic stays as-is for the flat case.
`pickResumeTarget` and `allCoursesComplete` continue to operate over the FULL course list, not per-section — the Continue Learning hero and "all complete" hero are unchanged.

Verify in browser using playwright-skill: with a fresh ~/.ai-lecturer/ (delete collections.json before the test if it exists — guard the test by writing to a temp HOME via a wrapper, OR back up + restore the real file in test setup/teardown), load `/`, screenshot — assert a `Widget Demos` section is present and contains AT LEAST 5 of the seeded slugs, the remaining (real) courses sit under `Uncategorized`. Click `[data-testid=collection-actions-<id>]` on Widget Demos, choose Rename, type `Demos`, screenshot — assert the heading text is now `Demos`. Click `[data-testid=course-card-move-pytorch-for-python-developers]`, choose `Demos`, screenshot — assert the pytorch card is now under Demos and gone from Uncategorized. Reload the page and assert state persisted (collection name `Demos`, pytorch still under it). Then DELETE the Demos collection via its kebab; reload; assert `collections: []` in /api/collections AND the seed does NOT re-run (Widget Demos heading does not reappear). Save all four screenshots under /tmp/ and reference paths in the progress report.
Out of scope: drag-and-drop reordering of courses or collections (move-to via menu only); nesting collections (flat list); per-collection accent overrides; sharing/exporting collections.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
stories.notes: Hard dependency on US-132. The seed gate is intentionally one-shot via the empty-store check — once the user touches collections, we never auto-add anything. window.prompt/window.confirm chosen over a custom modal to keep this story shippable in one ralph iteration; if the prompt/confirm UX feels too brutal a follow-up story can swap them for a styled modal.

stories.title: Sunset theme — token variant + 3-way ThemeToggle (Sun/Sunrise/Moon)
stories.description: As a user, I want a third 'sunset' theme alongside light/dark — a warm, low-contrast palette suitable for evening reading — and the existing top-bar theme button should cycle through all three states (light → sunset → dark → light) with a distinct icon for each, while the Settings menu's Theme group also offers Sunset as a selectable option alongside Light/Dark/System.
acceptanceCriteria: src/styles/tokens.css: add a new block `:root[data-theme="sunset"] { … }` that defines the SAME var names as the existing `:root[data-theme="dark"]` block but with a sunset palette: warm amber/terracotta-leaning surfaces, dimmed-but-not-black bg (e.g. `--bg: #2a1f1a; --bg-elevated: #332622; --bg-subtle: #3a2a25; --bg-hover: #44312a; --bg-active: #4f392f;`), warm-white text (`--text: #f4ddc0; --text-secondary: #d8b896; --text-tertiary: #b8967a;`), muted amber accent (`--accent: #e0a458; --accent-hover: #ebb573; --accent-active: #cc8e44; --accent-subtle: #2e2419; --accent-subtle-hover: #3a2c1f; --accent-border: #5a4628; --accent-text: #ebc183;`), warm danger/warning/insight/success kept readable. Mirror EVERY var declared in the dark block — do not omit any (`--widget-*`, `--code-*`, `--shadow-*`, `--shadow-focus`, etc.). The shadow set may copy the dark block as-is (warm transparent overlays still read fine on dark warm bg).

src/styles/tokens.css: add accent-variant overrides analogous to the existing `:root[data-theme="dark"][data-accent="<n>"]` blocks, for each of `default | black | indigo | terracotta | emerald` under `:root[data-theme="sunset"][data-accent="<n>"]`. Values may copy the dark variant for now (terracotta accent is an obvious aesthetic match for sunset; the others stay functional). This keeps the per-course accent system orthogonal to theme choice (US-076's contract).

src/components/SettingsMenu.tsx: change `type ThemePref = 'light' | 'dark' | 'system'` to `'light' | 'dark' | 'sunset' | 'system'`. Update the `readThemePref()` validity check, the `applyTheme()` switch (system stays mapped to light/dark via prefers-color-scheme — sunset is opt-in only, never auto), and append `{ value: 'sunset', label: 'Sunset' }` to `THEME_OPTIONS` (between `dark` and `system` so the cycle order in the menu mirrors the toggle cycle order).

src/components/ThemeToggle.tsx: change `type Theme = 'light' | 'dark'` to `'light' | 'dark' | 'sunset'`. `readTheme()` reads the data-theme attribute and returns `'sunset'` when the attr is `'sunset'`, otherwise the existing light/dark branch. Replace the `toggle` two-state flip with a three-way cycle: `light → sunset → dark → light`. Persist to THEME_STORAGE_KEY (which now accepts the `'sunset'` literal — the SettingsMenu validity check already covers it).

src/components/ThemeToggle.tsx: import `Sunrise` from `lucide-react` (the sunset/sunrise glyph; if `Sunrise` isn't exported in the installed lucide-react version, fall back to `SunMedium` or `SunDim` — check the actual exports and pick whichever sunset-leaning icon exists). The icon stack now layers three icons (`Sun` for dark→light cue, `Sunrise` for sunset, `Moon` for light/sunset→dark cue) with opacity transitions identical to the existing two-icon pattern, so the visible icon at any moment is: when current theme is `light` → show `Moon` (next-state hint, matches existing behavior); when `sunset` → show `Sunrise`; when `dark` → show `Sun`. Update aria-label accordingly: light → 'Switch to sunset mode', sunset → 'Switch to dark mode', dark → 'Switch to light mode'.

src/app/layout.tsx (or the file that hosts the inline boot script — locate via grep for `THEME_STORAGE_KEY` literal `'aiLecturer.theme'`): the boot script's parsing of the persisted theme value must accept `'sunset'` as a valid value and apply `data-theme="sunset"` BEFORE first paint. Invalid/missing → keep existing default (system → matches prefers-color-scheme).

Existing tests for SettingsMenu / ThemeToggle: extend (do not delete) to cover the cycle `light → sunset → dark → light` (assert ThemeToggle clicks update both `<html data-theme>` and the persisted localStorage value) and that selecting `Sunset` in SettingsMenu applies `data-theme="sunset"`.

Verify in browser using playwright-skill: load `/test-theme` (the existing token-verification route from US-002), evaluate `document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme','sunset')`, screenshot — assert bg/text colors are visibly warm (not the cool dark grays), accent button is still legible. Then load `/`, click `[data-testid=theme-toggle]` once from the default state and screenshot the resulting theme; click again and screenshot; click again and screenshot — three captures showing the three states with three distinct icons. Reference all four screenshot paths in the progress report.
Out of scope: a fourth 'system'-aware sunset (auto-switch to sunset at dusk based on local time) — sunset stays an explicit user choice; per-course default sunset; high-contrast variant of sunset.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
stories.notes: Palette values above are a starting point — the iteration agent may tune saturations/lightnesses to keep WCAG AA contrast on text vs bg, but MUST keep the core warm/amber identity (no sneaking back to neutral grays). The 3-way ThemeToggle cycle vs Settings-menu radio is intentional — both are equally valid entry points; the toggle is a one-click cycle for power users, the menu is the declarative picker.

stories.title: AI Tutor chat — resizable via left-edge drag handle
stories.description: As a learner with a wide display, I want to grab the left edge of the open AI Tutor chat panel and drag it wider (or narrower) so I can give long tutor responses more breathing room without expanding to the fullscreen overlay. The chat lives in the lesson grid's third column at a fixed 320px (page.tsx:97 `CHAT_OPEN = 320`) — make that width user-controlled and persisted.
acceptanceCriteria: src/app/courses/[slug]/lessons/[lessonSlug]/page.tsx: replace the constant `CHAT_OPEN = 320` with state `chatWidth` initialized via a new `readChatWidth()` helper that reads `localStorage['lessonChat-width']`, parses as int, clamps to [280, 720], defaults to 320 on missing/invalid. Mirror the existing `lessonChat-open` persistence pattern (`CHAT_OPEN_KEY`) — add a sibling constant `CHAT_WIDTH_KEY = 'lessonChat-width'`. The grid template columns formula at page.tsx:396 changes from `${chatCol}px` (where chatCol was 320) to `${chatOpen ? chatWidth : 0}px`.

Add a drag-handle div at the LEFT edge of the LessonChat aside (rendered inside src/components/LessonChat.tsx in the non-expanded state ONLY — when the chat is in fullscreen overlay mode via `asideExpandedStyle`, the handle is hidden because the panel is no longer in the grid). The handle is absolutely positioned at `left: 0; top: 0; bottom: 0; width: 6px; cursor: col-resize;` with `data-testid="lesson-chat-resize-handle"`. On hover/active it shows a faint accent color (`background: var(--accent-subtle)` on hover, `var(--accent)` while dragging).

Drag interaction: `onPointerDown` on the handle captures the pointer (`e.currentTarget.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId)`), `onPointerMove` computes `newWidth = clamp(window.innerWidth - e.clientX, 280, 720)` and reports it upward via a new `onResize?: (w: number) => void` prop on LessonChat. The lesson page wires `onResize={setChatWidth}` so the grid re-templates live (via the existing `transition: 'grid-template-columns 180ms ease'` — though for live-drag responsiveness, the parent ALSO disables that transition while a drag is active by toggling a `dragging` flag that swaps to `transition: 'none'`; transition restored on pointer-up so close/open animations still ease). On `onPointerUp`, the handle releases capture and the lesson page persists the final width to localStorage AND dispatches no SETTINGS_CHANGE_EVENT (this is per-lesson-page state, not a global setting).

Touch + keyboard fallback: the handle is also focusable (`tabIndex={0}`, `role="separator"`, `aria-orientation="vertical"`, `aria-valuemin="280" aria-valuemax="720" aria-valuenow={chatWidth}`). Left/Right arrow keys adjust width by 16px per press, Shift+Arrow by 64px. Each keypress also persists.

Edge cases: when the user resizes the browser to <600px wide, clamp the effective width to `min(chatWidth, window.innerWidth - 320)` so the lesson column still has at least 320px to render — no persistence on this clamp (the user's persisted preference is preserved for when they widen the window again). When the chat is closed (`chatOpen === false`), the persisted width is irrelevant — reopening restores the persisted width.

Verify in browser using playwright-skill: load /courses/widget-dev-guide/lessons/<first lesson> at 1280px viewport, open the AI tutor (existing `[data-testid=tutor-btn]`), screenshot — chat at default 320px. Programmatically dispatch a sequence of pointerdown / pointermove / pointerup events on `[data-testid=lesson-chat-resize-handle]` to drag the handle 200px to the LEFT (i.e., `clientX` decreasing → width increasing to ~520px), screenshot — chat panel visibly wider, lesson stream visibly narrower. Reload the page; screenshot — chat reopens at 520px (persistence verified). Reset by dragging back to ~320 and reload to confirm the new value also persists. Reference three screenshot paths in the progress report.

Out of scope: resizing the chat from the right edge while in fullscreen overlay mode (overlay is an explicit fullscreen state — exit it first); resizing the TOC column (not requested); per-course chat-width preferences; horizontal drag on touch devices via two-finger gesture (single-finger drag on the handle is already covered by pointer events).
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
stories.notes: The chat aside's grid placement (`gridColumn: '3 / 4'`) and the lesson page's grid-template-columns are the only layout primitives that need to know the new width — everything else inside LessonChat already flexes via `width: '100%'` and `minWidth: 0`. The 280/720 bounds are conservative: 280 keeps the composer + send button readable, 720 keeps the lesson column from collapsing on a 1280px viewport (1280 - 720 - 276 (TOC expanded) = 284px lesson column — narrow but still legible). Adjust upward only if user requests later.

stories.title: Persist per-course generation state to .generation-state.json
stories.description: As the course-generation backend, I want a per-course `.generation-state.json` file updated atomically on every stage transition so a subsequent restart or resume can recover exactly which lessons are done, in flight, or pending — without re-running completed work or losing the attempt count of in-flight retries. Foundation for the auto-resume work in US-137 / US-140. The current `.generating.json` marker (see src/lib/server/generation.ts:239 `GENERATING_MARKER`) only records `{ childPid, slug, stage, startedAt }`, which is enough for the US-106 resume banner but not enough to actually resume — there's no per-lesson status, no attempt count, no record of the run config.
acceptanceCriteria: New module src/lib/server/generationState.ts exports `GenerationStateSchema` (Zod): `{ schemaVersion: z.literal(1), slug: z.string(), startedAt: z.string(), lastUpdatedAt: z.string(), initCourse: z.object({ status: z.enum(['pending','done','failed']), reason: z.string().optional() }), lessons: z.array(z.object({ slug: z.string(), status: z.enum(['pending','inflight','done','failed']), attempts: z.number().int().nonnegative(), lastError: z.string().optional(), finishedAt: z.string().optional() })), config: z.object({ lessonMaxRetries: z.number().int().nonnegative(), lessonTimeoutMs: z.number().int().positive() }) }`. Export inferred type `GenerationState`.

src/lib/server/generationState.ts also exports: `generationStateFile(slug): string` (returns `<courseDir>/.generation-state.json` via the existing `courseDir` helper from src/lib/server/paths.ts); `readGenerationState(slug): Promise<GenerationState | null>` (returns null on ENOENT, parses + validates via the schema, returns null on parse/validation error after logging a single warning to stderr); `writeGenerationState(slug, state): Promise<void>` (atomic write via the existing src/lib/server/atomic.ts helper, sets `lastUpdatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` before writing); `deleteGenerationState(slug): Promise<void>` (best-effort unlink; swallow ENOENT).

src/lib/server/generation.ts wires the writes into the pipeline: at startGenerationInner, after course.json is read (or right after init_course's stage:done writes it), write the initial state — `initCourse: { status: 'pending' }` if init still running otherwise 'done'; `lessons: course.modules.flatMap(m => m.lessons).map(l => ({ slug: l.slug, status: 'pending', attempts: 0 }))`; `config` populated from the resolved lessonMaxRetries / lessonTimeoutMs. Update the state file at: init_course `stage:started` (no-op if already pending), init_course `stage:done` (initCourse.status = 'done'), init_course `stage:error` (initCourse.status = 'failed', initCourse.reason = error message); per-lesson before each spawn (status = 'inflight', attempts++); per-lesson after schema validation success (status = 'done', finishedAt = now); per-lesson after attempts exhausted (status = 'failed', lastError = reason).

finalize() is updated: on `kind === 'done'` with no failed lessons → call `deleteGenerationState(slug)` (success path — state file removed); on `kind === 'done'` with failedLessons.length > 0 OR on `kind === 'error'` → leave the state file in place (resume target). The existing `removeGeneratingMarker(slug)` call is preserved unchanged — the new state file is independent of the existing marker.

Unit tests in src/lib/server/generationState.test.ts: read on missing file returns null; read on corrupt JSON returns null + emits exactly one warn (use `vi.spyOn(console, 'warn')`); write+read roundtrip; lastUpdatedAt is set on write; deleteGenerationState on missing file is a no-op. Tests use a temp courses root via the existing COURSES_ROOT_OVERRIDE env mechanism.

Integration tests in src/lib/server/generation.test.ts (extend, do not duplicate): pipeline run with a mock claude that succeeds → state file is written during init, updated through each lesson, and DELETED on full success; pipeline run with a mock claude that fails one lesson after exhausting retries → state file is left in place with that lesson's status='failed' and lastError set; concurrent kill-9 of the child mid-lesson does not corrupt the file (atomic write guarantees no .tmp leftover).

Out of scope: actually USING the state for resume (US-137 owns it); UI surfacing (US-140 owns it); SSE replay using a different file (US-138 owns it); migration of pre-existing `.generating.json` markers (the new file is additive — old runs still surface via the existing reconciliation path until they finalize).
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
stories.notes: Foundation story — US-137 and US-140 both depend on this file existing. Schema deliberately small (no event log here — that's US-138's ndjson). Atomic write reuses src/lib/server/atomic.ts (same helper as progress.json and course.json). The state file lives inside the course directory (not under ~/.ai-lecturer/) so a `rm -rf courses/<slug>` cleans up everything related to the run.

stories.title: Resume in-flight generation: skip done lessons, preserve attempt counts
stories.description: As a user whose server crashed mid-generation (or who returns to /create with the US-106 resume banner showing), I want the partial run to actually pick up where it left off — completed lessons not regenerated, the in-flight lesson retried with its remaining attempt budget, pending lessons run normally — instead of silently restarting from scratch and burning tokens. Today the `Resume generation` action effectively re-POSTs to /api/courses/generate which calls enqueueGeneration → startGeneration → full pipeline from init_course onwards. Builds on US-136's `.generation-state.json`.
acceptanceCriteria: New exported function `resumeGeneration(slug, depsArg?: SpawnDeps): Promise<GenerationRun>` in src/lib/server/generation.ts. Reads `.generation-state.json` via readGenerationState from US-136; throws a new `GenerationStateMissingError` (extends Error, name = 'GenerationStateMissingError') when the file is absent.

Pipeline behavior: if `initCourse.status !== 'done'` → re-runs init_course like a fresh pipeline (and re-derives the lesson list from course.json on init success, merging into existing state by slug — preserves attempt counts for any lessons already begun). If `initCourse.status === 'done'` → skips the init spawn entirely. Iterates `state.lessons[]`: skips lessons with `status === 'done'`; for `inflight` / `failed` / `pending` runs `claude -p generate_lesson` with remaining attempt budget computed as `max(0, state.config.lessonMaxRetries + 1 - existing.attempts)`. If a lesson's remaining budget is 0, mark it failed and continue (don't spawn).

Stale .tmp cleanup: before each lesson attempt, unlink any `<courseDir>/lessons/<lessonSlug>.tmp` from a prior atomic-write crash (best-effort, ignore ENOENT). Cleanup leaves any sibling valid `<lessonSlug>.json` untouched — only the .tmp variant is removed.

SSE: as the FIRST event after the run is registered (before any other stage events), emit `{ type: 'resumed', completed: string[], remaining: string[], inflightSlug: string | null }` so the wizard can hydrate its lesson-status panel in one round-trip. `completed` = lessons with status='done'; `remaining` = the rest in source order; `inflightSlug` = first lesson currently being attempted (or null if the resume starts at init). Update the GenerationEvent union in generation.ts to include this variant; update the SSE route to forward it like any other event.

New POST route at src/app/api/courses/[slug]/resume/route.ts. Returns `{ runId: string }` (matching the existing /api/courses/generate response shape). On GenerationStateMissingError → 409 with `{ error: 'no-resumable-state' }`. On GenerationConflictError (a different slug is already active) → 409 with `{ error: 'busy' }`. Same slug already active → idempotent attach (return existing runId), mirroring enqueueGeneration's behavior.

enqueueGeneration is unchanged — resume is a separate code path. The wizard / banner UI from US-140 will choose between POST /api/courses/<slug>/resume (when state exists) and POST /api/courses/generate (fresh start) explicitly.

Unit/integration tests in src/lib/server/generation.test.ts: drive a mock claude that succeeds for lessons 1, 3 and fails for lesson 2 (no exhaustion) → kill the child after lesson 1 completes via the existing test harness; resume → only lessons 2 and 3 spawn (lesson 1 skipped), attempt counts on lesson 2 continue from where they left off. Resume with state showing lesson 2 attempts=3 and lessonMaxRetries=2 → lesson 2 immediately marked failed, lesson 3 still runs. Resume with no state file → throws GenerationStateMissingError. Stale .tmp file in lessons/ is removed before the spawn; valid sibling .json is untouched.
Route tests: POST /api/courses/<slug>/resume with a state file present → 200 + runId; without state file → 409 no-resumable-state; while another slug is active → 409 busy.

Out of scope: UI changes (US-140 owns the resume banner button rewiring); restoring SSE event scrollback for previously-emitted events (US-138 owns ndjson + replay); auto-firing resume on server boot without user action (deliberately deferred — the boot drainer was considered and dropped).
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
stories.notes: Hard dependency on US-136. The `resumed` SSE event is intentionally distinct from `progress` so the UI can render a one-shot hydration panel without conflating it with live tick updates. The 'init not done' branch deliberately re-runs init_course rather than trying to recover partial init state — init writes course.json + research.md + sources.md atomically, so either it ran to completion or it didn't, and re-running is safe.

stories.title: Persistent generation events as ndjson + SSE Last-Event-ID replay
stories.description: As a UI client connecting to the SSE generation stream, I want a reconnect (network blip, tab restore, server restart) to replay events since my last seen event-id so the wizard's log scrollback survives without gaps or duplicates. Today GenerationRun.events is in-memory only; on server restart all SSE ids become invalid and a reconnect mid-run sees only events from the moment of reconnect.
acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/server/generation.ts: every emitted GenerationEvent is appended to `<courseDir>/.generation-events.ndjson` BEFORE notifying in-memory listeners. Each line is a JSON object: `{ seq: number, timestamp: string, event: GenerationEvent }`. `seq` is monotonically increasing per run, starting at 1; persisted in-memory on the GenerationRun and reset on each new pipeline (resume continues incrementing from where the previous run left off when the ndjson file is still present).

Rotation: when the active ndjson file exceeds 5 MB (check via fs.stat after each write — cheap), rename it to `.generation-events.<startedAt>.ndjson` and start a fresh `.generation-events.ndjson`. Replay only reads the active file; rotated files are kept on disk for forensics but not surfaced to clients. Use the existing atomic.ts helper for the rename, not for the append (appends are not atomic — small partial-line risk is acceptable for an event log; the parser skips malformed lines).

SSE handler at src/app/api/courses/generate/stream/[runId]/route.ts (locate via grep — current path may differ): accept the standard `Last-Event-ID` request header (a stringified seq number) AND a `?from=<seq>` query parameter (header takes precedence when both present). On request, read the active ndjson, replay events with `seq > from` synchronously to the client (each as a `data:` chunk with a matching `id:` line), THEN attach the live in-memory listener. Race-free: take a snapshot of `run.events.length` AFTER opening the stream but BEFORE replaying, then skip in-memory events whose seq is <= the last replayed seq.

Each emitted SSE chunk includes a separate `id: <seq>
` line so the browser's EventSource populates `Last-Event-ID` automatically on reconnect. The existing `data: <json>

` framing is preserved.

Malformed lines (truncated by partial write at crash) are skipped during replay without throwing. A counter logs once per replay if any lines were skipped (`console.warn('[gen] skipped N malformed lines in events log')`); production never sees this if the process exits cleanly.

Unit tests in src/lib/server/generation.test.ts: write 100 events to a run, capture seq=42, simulate disconnect, request replay with Last-Event-ID=42 → next event seen is seq=43 and there are no duplicates; trigger a rotation by writing > 5 MB of events, request replay from a seq before the rotation → only events from the active file are returned (rotated content is intentionally NOT replayed); inject a malformed line in the middle of the active file → replay skips it and continues.

Out of scope: replay across rotated files (clients reconnecting after a multi-MB run gap may miss old scrollback — that's the rotation contract); compressing the rotated logs; a CLI tool to inspect rotated logs.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
stories.notes: ndjson append is best-effort by design — atomic write per-line would dominate I/O cost on a 12-lesson generation that emits hundreds of stream-json events per lesson. The malformed-line skip handles the rare partial-write at process kill. The 5 MB cap protects against runaway logs from a chatty `claude -p stream-json` run; rotating once gives at most ~10 MB on disk per run before manual cleanup.

stories.title: Skip lesson generation when valid <lessonSlug>.json already exists
stories.description: As a defensive guard on the generation pipeline, before invoking `claude -p generate_lesson` for any lesson, the pipeline should check whether `/courses/<slug>/lessons/<lessonSlug>.json` already exists and validates against LessonSchema — and if so, mark it done and skip the spawn. Protects against wasted token spend on resumes (US-137), manual file copies, partial-success replays, or any other case where the file already represents valid work. Cheap, decoupled, can ship before US-136.
acceptanceCriteria: New helper `isLessonAlreadyValid(slug, lessonSlug): Promise<{ valid: true; lesson: Lesson } | { valid: false; reason: 'missing' | 'parse-error' | 'schema-error' }>` in src/lib/server/generation.ts (or a new src/lib/server/lessonValidation.ts if it tidies the file). Reads via fs.readFile (returns `{ valid: false, reason: 'missing' }` on ENOENT), parses JSON (returns `{ valid: false, reason: 'parse-error' }` on parse error), runs LessonSchema.safeParse from src/lib/schemas/lesson.ts (returns `{ valid: false, reason: 'schema-error' }` when success=false). Schema validation is the same one used by the per-lesson route handler, ensuring idempotency-by-file aligns with the API's notion of validity.

Pipeline integration: at the start of each lesson's loop iteration in startGenerationInner, call isLessonAlreadyValid. On `{ valid: true }`: emit a `stage:started` and immediately `stage:done` event with `name: lesson:<lessonSlug>` (so the SSE log shows it as completed); increment the progress counter; emit a `progress` event; skip the spawn entirely. On `{ valid: false }` (any reason): existing behavior (run claude -p), preceded by a stale-tmp cleanup (unlink `<lessonSlug>.tmp` if present).

When US-136's state file exists, the pre-skip path also writes `status='done', attempts=0, finishedAt=now` for that lesson via writeGenerationState. When the state file does not exist (US-136 not yet shipped, or the legacy path), the pre-skip behavior still works — the state file write is conditional on readGenerationState returning non-null.
Stale-tmp cleanup is its own unlink call independent of the validity check (covers the case where both `<lessonSlug>.json` (valid) AND `<lessonSlug>.tmp` exist — the .tmp is dropped regardless).

Unit/integration tests in src/lib/server/generation.test.ts: pre-place a valid lesson JSON for `lesson-a` before pipeline start (via fs.writeFile in test setup) → pipeline run with a mock claude is observed to NOT be invoked for `lesson-a` (use the existing spawn-mock to assert command invocations); pre-place an invalid (truncated) lesson JSON → mock claude IS invoked, the bad file is overwritten with the new valid one; pre-place a JSON missing required fields per LessonSchema → same as truncated; pre-place a stale `lesson-a.tmp` alongside a valid `lesson-a.json` → tmp removed, no spawn for lesson-a; pre-place a stale `lesson-b.tmp` only → tmp removed and spawn proceeds.
Integration test: a 3-lesson course where lessons 1 and 3 are pre-placed valid, lesson 2 is missing → spawn count = 1 (only lesson 2), final progress = 3/3, all `stage:done` events emitted correctly.

Out of scope: validating course.json idempotency at init (init already overwrites; not a token-saver); checksumming lesson JSON for byte-identity (LessonSchema validity is the contract); recovering partially-corrupt course state where some lessons reference modules that don't match course.json (out of scope — addressed by re-running init).
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
stories.notes: Smallest of the auto-resume stories and the most defensive — can ship independently of US-136 / US-137 and pay off immediately on any subsequent run. The 'parse-error vs schema-error' distinction in the return type is a future-proofing affordance — current callers treat both the same (re-spawn) but a future story might want different telemetry per failure mode.

stories.title: Resume-generation banner: per-lesson dots + 'cancel and restart' option
stories.description: As a user returning to /create after a crash or refresh with a partial generation in progress, I want the resume banner from US-106 to show concrete progress — N of M lessons done, which one is in flight, which are pending — and offer a 'cancel and restart from scratch' option alongside the existing Resume action, so I can decide whether to continue or abandon the partial run instead of being limited to a binary 'continue?' button.
acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/server/generation.ts: extend the `ActiveRunSummary` type for the `active: true` variant with an optional `progress?: { initStatus: 'pending'|'done'|'failed', lessonsDone: number, lessonsTotal: number, currentLessonSlug: string | null, lessons: Array<{ slug: string, title: string, status: 'pending'|'inflight'|'done'|'failed' }> }`. computeActiveRunSummary attempts to read .generation-state.json (US-136) — when present, populate `progress` from it (cross-referencing course.json for the lesson titles); when absent, omit the field entirely (older runs / pre-US-136 state remain compatible).
src/app/api/courses/active-run/route.ts: passes the new `progress` field through unchanged in its JSON response. No additional validation — the field is server-generated.

src/app/create/page.tsx resume banner (locate via grep for 'resume' or the component name introduced by US-106): when `progress` is present, render a horizontal lesson-dot strip directly under the banner title. Each dot is a 10px circle with 4px gap; colors via CSS vars: `pending → var(--text-tertiary)`, `inflight → var(--accent)` with a subtle pulse animation (CSS @keyframes pulse 1.4s linear infinite; respect prefers-reduced-motion → static), `done → var(--success)`, `failed → var(--danger)`. Each dot has `title="<lesson title>"` for hover tooltip; clicking a `done` dot opens `/courses/<slug>/lessons/<lessonSlug>` in a new tab (target=_blank, rel=noopener). Above the dots, show `<lessonsDone> of <lessonsTotal> lessons · <currentLessonSlug or '—'>` text in --text-secondary --fs-sm.

Banner buttons: primary action remains `Resume generation` but now POSTs to `/api/courses/<slug>/resume` (US-137) when `progress` is present (state file exists), falling back to POST `/api/courses/generate` when `progress` is absent. The fetch error handler shows a toast on 409 `no-resumable-state` (race: state was deleted between summary and click — fall back to fresh generate after a short delay) and 409 `busy` (different course is mid-flight — disabled with explanatory tooltip).

Banner secondary action: a new ghost button `Cancel and restart` (`data-testid="cancel-and-restart-btn"`). Click opens window.confirm with the message 'This will delete the partial generation and any lessons already produced for <course title>. Continue?'. On confirm, fire DELETE `/api/courses/<slug>/generation-state` (new route — see next AC) → on 204 success, immediately POST `/api/courses/generate` for a fresh run; on failure, show an error toast.

New DELETE route at src/app/api/courses/[slug]/generation-state/route.ts: deletes (best-effort) the per-course `.generation-state.json`, `.generating.json`, `.generation-events.ndjson`, the `.generation-events.*.ndjson` rotated files, AND every file under `<courseDir>/lessons/`. course.json / course-spec.json / research.md / sources.md / sources/ uploads / logs/ remain untouched (init artifacts may be reused by the fresh run; the user did not opt to delete the entire course). Returns 204 on success, 409 if a generation is currently active for that slug (the user must cancel via existing flow first), 400 on slug-traversal attempts. Slug-validation reuses assertSafeSlug from src/lib/server/paths.ts.

Verify in browser using playwright-skill: pre-seed via fs.writeFile a `.generation-state.json` for a 4-lesson mock course (course.json with 4 lesson slugs, state file with lessons[0].status='done', lessons[1].status='inflight', lessons[2..3].status='pending') and matching `.generating.json` with a fake-but-alive PID (use process.pid of the test harness so isPidAlive returns true). Load `/create`, screenshot — assert the banner shows `1 of 4 lessons · <inflight-slug>` AND four dots in colors [done, inflight, pending, pending]. Click `Cancel and restart` and accept the confirm dialog → screenshot — assert /courses/<slug>/lessons/ is empty and the banner is gone (no active run). Reference both screenshots in the progress report.

Out of scope: showing rotated event-log files in the UI (US-138 keeps rotated files on disk, not in UI); a finer-grained 'cancel only this lesson' control (full-restart only); a preflight summary listing the modules whose lessons would be deleted (the confirm message is intentionally short — power users can inspect /courses/<slug>/lessons/ via shell if they want a full preview).
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
stories.notes: Hard dependency on US-136 (state file) and on US-137 (resume route). Without those, the banner gracefully degrades to today's behavior (the existing button + no progress dots). The Cancel-and-restart button uses window.confirm rather than a custom modal to keep this story shippable in one ralph iteration — same trade-off as US-133.

stories.title: Cross-lesson coherence pass: final-stage agent + coherence-report.md
stories.description: As a course author, after a full course generation completes I want a final coherence pass that audits the generated lessons as a set — checking prerequisite ordering, redundancy across lessons, and notational consistency — and writes a human-readable report I can use to decide which lessons (if any) to regenerate.
acceptanceCriteria: New skill at scripts/ralph/skills/coherence_pass/coherence_pass.md describing the agent's role: read course.json + every lesson JSON under /courses/<slug>/lessons/, then output a markdown report with three named sections — `## Prerequisite Order` (lessons that depend on concepts not yet introduced), `## Redundancy` (concepts re-explained across lessons without acknowledgement), `## Notation Consistency` (variable names, symbols, conventions that drift). Skill emits ONLY the markdown text — no JSON wrapper.

Generation pipeline integration in src/lib/server/generation.ts: after the last per-lesson `claude -p generate_lesson` invocation succeeds AND every lesson is on disk + valid (existing US-139 logic), run a final stage `coherence-pass`. Spawn `claude -p` with the coherence_pass skill, passing the course slug as cwd context, capture stdout, write to `/courses/<slug>/coherence-report.md`. The stage emits `stage:started` with `name: 'coherence-pass'` and `stage:done` (or `stage:failed`) like other stages so the live log shows it. Failure of this stage does NOT mark the course generation as failed — the report is best-effort; emit `stage:failed` with the error and continue.

When coherence pass succeeds, the response of GET /api/courses/<slug>/active-run includes a final `coherenceReportPath` field on completion summary (relative path `coherence-report.md`); when it fails, the field is absent and the failure is visible only in the SSE event log. Out of scope: surfacing the report in the UI (US can land later as a separate story); auto-rerunning lessons based on findings (explicitly out of scope per product decision).

When `RALPH_TASK_ID` env or any other ralph orchestrator env is detected (i.e. running headless inside an iteration), still execute the pass — but cap stdout consumption with a 30s timeout per spawn, and write `Coherence pass timed out — re-run generation to retry.` to the report on timeout. This protects iteration budgets without silently skipping.

Unit/integration tests in src/lib/server/generation.test.ts: with a 3-lesson mocked course where all lessons are pre-placed valid, run startGenerationInner with a mocked spawn — assert the final spawn command is the coherence_pass skill (not generate_lesson), assert `coherence-report.md` is written from the mock stdout, assert `stage:done` event with name `coherence-pass` appears AFTER all lesson stages. Failure test: mocked coherence spawn returns non-zero → `stage:failed` is emitted, course generation still completes (existing lessons remain), no `coherence-report.md` is written.

Out of scope: cross-course coherence (only within one course); per-module coherence checks (final pass only — product decision); UI surfacing of the report (file is on disk for now); auto-fix loops (read-only audit).
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

stories.title: Extend course: agent skill + POST /api/courses/<slug>/extend
stories.description: As a course author, I want a server-side extend agent that takes my existing course schema (with lesson descriptions) plus a free-text instruction describing what I want to add, and returns a proposed extended schema marking which modules and lessons are new — without yet committing changes to disk or generating any lesson content. This story delivers the backend: a skill .md, a POST endpoint, and the structured response shape that downstream UI stories (US-144, US-145) consume.
acceptanceCriteria: New skill at scripts/ralph/skills/extend_course/extend_course.md describing the agent: input is a JSON block with `currentSchema` (full course.json with module/lesson titles + descriptions) + `instruction` (user free-text) + optional `refinements: Array<{ role: 'user', content: string }>` (chat-history for iterative refinement, used by US-145). Output MUST be a single JSON object emitted on stdout: `{ proposedSchema: <full course schema with modules+lessons including any newly added>, additions: { newModuleIds: string[], newLessonIds: { moduleId: string, lessonSlug: string, lessonTitle: string, lessonDescription: string }[], rationale: string } }`. Skill instructs the agent to PRESERVE all existing module/lesson IDs and titles unchanged — additions only.

New POST /api/courses/[slug]/extend/route.ts handler: body validated by Zod schema `{ instruction: string (1..2000 chars), refinements?: Array<{ role: 'user', content: string (1..2000) }> (max 10) }`. Reads /courses/<slug>/course.json + every lesson JSON's description field, builds skill input JSON, spawns `claude -p extend_course` (reusing the existing spawnClaude helper from src/lib/server/generation.ts), captures stdout, parses as JSON, validates against ExtendResponseSchema, returns it. Returns 400 on invalid body, 404 on missing slug, 422 on agent-output parse failure (with the raw stdout truncated to 2KB in the error message for debugging), 500 on spawn failure.

ExtendResponseSchema (new file src/lib/schemas/extend.ts): proposedSchema reuses the existing CourseSchema from src/lib/schemas/course.ts; additions is its own object schema. Schema is exported and used both by the route handler and consumed by the future UI story.

Endpoint is purely read-only-from-disk: it does NOT write course.json, does NOT trigger generation, does NOT modify lesson files. (A separate Apply endpoint added in US-144 handles persistence.) This isolates risk: the agent can be called repeatedly without side effects.

Reuses the existing computeActiveRunSummary check: if a generation is currently active for the slug, return 409 with `{ error: 'busy', message: 'Cannot extend while generation is active' }` — extending a course mid-generation would corrupt state.

Unit tests in src/app/api/courses/[slug]/extend/route.test.ts (or src/lib/server/extend.test.ts if a helper module is extracted): with a mock of spawnClaude, verify that valid input → valid response is parsed and returned; invalid agent stdout (non-JSON, schema-mismatched) → 422 with parse error; missing course → 404; busy state → 409.

Out of scope: any UI (US-144 + US-145); the Apply endpoint (US-144); modifying course.json or generating new lessons (US-144 Apply triggers that); persisting refinement chat history server-side (refinements are passed in by the client each call — stateless server).
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
stories.notes: Stateless agent design (refinements passed in per call) deliberately keeps US-143 small and side-effect-free. The Apply step lives in US-144 because it touches course.json + generation pipeline — separation lets US-143 ship and be tested in isolation.

stories.title: Regenerate section: skill + POST /api/courses/<slug>/lessons/<lessonSlug>/sections/<sectionId>/regenerate
stories.description: As a course author reviewing a generated lesson, I want a server-side regenerate-section flow that takes a single section + a short user instruction (e.g., "more code-focused", "shorter", "add a comparison") and returns a regenerated version of that section, leaving the rest of the lesson untouched. This story delivers the backend skill + endpoint; the UI (with highlighted-additions preview) lives in US-147.
acceptanceCriteria: New skill at scripts/ralph/skills/regenerate_section/regenerate_section.md describing the agent: input is a JSON block with `lessonContext` (full Lesson JSON), `sectionId` (string), and `instruction` (user free-text 1..1000). Output MUST be a single JSON object on stdout: `{ newSection: <Section conforming to SectionSchema with same id+kind as input section but new content> }`. Skill instructs the agent to PRESERVE the section's `id` and `kind` (theory stays theory, quiz stays quiz, etc.) — only `content`/`prompt`/widget-specific fields may change.

New POST /api/courses/[slug]/lessons/[lessonSlug]/sections/[sectionId]/regenerate/route.ts handler: body Zod-validated as `{ instruction: string (1..1000) }`. Reads /courses/<slug>/lessons/<lessonSlug>.json, locates the section by id (404 if not found), spawns `claude -p regenerate_section` with the skill input JSON, captures stdout, parses + validates as `{ newSection: SectionSchema }` ensuring newSection.id === sectionId and newSection.kind === oldSection.kind (rejects with 422 if either drifted), returns `{ newSection, oldSection }`. Does NOT write to disk in this story — preview is computed client-side; persisting happens via a follow-up Apply call (next AC).

Companion POST /api/courses/[slug]/lessons/[lessonSlug]/sections/[sectionId]/apply/route.ts: body `{ newSection: SectionSchema }`. Re-validates the section, re-asserts id+kind preservation against the on-disk lesson, replaces only that section in the lessons array, writes lesson.json. Returns 200 with the updated Lesson. Returns 422 on validation failure, 404 if the lesson or section is missing. (A separate route to keep state changes explicit and resilient against the regen route having side effects.)
Both routes return 409 if a generation is currently active for the slug.

ParamSchema validation for slug, lessonSlug, sectionId — reuse assertSafeSlug for slug+lessonSlug; sectionId is the lesson's internal id, validated by checking it exists in the lesson (no path-traversal risk since it's not used in fs paths).

Tests pass

stories.title: Regenerate lesson: skill + POST /api/courses/<slug>/lessons/<lessonSlug>/regenerate with .lesson-prev.json snapshot
stories.description: As a course author dissatisfied with a whole lesson, I want a regenerate-lesson backend that snapshots the current lesson.json before overwriting it with a fresh agent-generated version per a user instruction, so a one-step Undo (US-149) can restore the prior version. The agent receives the user instruction, the course schema, and the current lesson content as context, and outputs a new full Lesson JSON.
acceptanceCriteria: New skill at scripts/ralph/skills/regenerate_lesson/regenerate_lesson.md: input JSON contains `courseSchema` (course.json), `currentLesson` (full Lesson JSON), `instruction` (user free-text 1..2000). Output MUST be a single JSON on stdout: `{ newLesson: <Lesson conforming to LessonSchema with same slug+title as input> }`. Skill instructs agent to preserve lesson.slug, lesson.title, and the lesson's parent moduleId; section ids may change (full regeneration) but the section count + kinds should remain reasonable for the lesson's purpose (no hard constraint on section ids since the whole lesson is regenerated).

New POST /api/courses/[slug]/lessons/[lessonSlug]/regenerate/route.ts handler: body Zod-validated as `{ instruction: string (1..2000) }`. Reads /courses/<slug>/course.json + /courses/<slug>/lessons/<lessonSlug>.json. Spawns `claude -p regenerate_lesson` with the skill input JSON. On success: writes the existing lesson.json byte-for-byte to /courses/<slug>/lessons/<lessonSlug>.lesson-prev.json (overwriting any prior snapshot — only ONE level of undo by design), then writes the parsed+validated newLesson to lesson.json, returns `{ newLesson, hasUndo: true }`. On agent-output validation failure → 422, lesson.json untouched, no snapshot written. On 409 busy → reject. Slug+lessonSlug validated via assertSafeSlug.

Companion POST /api/courses/[slug]/lessons/[lessonSlug]/regenerate/undo/route.ts: returns 404 if `<lessonSlug>.lesson-prev.json` doesn't exist, otherwise restores it onto lesson.json (rename or copy+delete), deletes the snapshot afterwards, returns 200 with `{ restoredLesson }`. After undo there is no further undo (single-step by design — explicit and predictable).

Snapshot policy: ONLY regenerate-lesson writes the .lesson-prev.json snapshot. Section regenerate (US-147) does NOT write to it (would clobber a real lesson-undo). Manual edits via the lesson editor (existing) do NOT write to it. The snapshot represents 'the lesson before the most recent full regenerate' specifically.

Snapshot file is gitignored at the courses subdirectory level (or added to /courses/.gitignore if it exists, else the project .gitignore via a `*.lesson-prev.json` pattern). Verify the existing .gitignore is updated.

Unit/integration tests: mock spawnClaude returning a deterministic newLesson; pre-place a lesson.json with content X; POST regenerate with instruction → assert newLesson written, .lesson-prev.json contains X byte-identical, response.hasUndo === true. POST undo → assert lesson.json now contains X, .lesson-prev.json deleted. Edge: POST undo when no snapshot exists → 404. Edge: regenerate twice in a row → second regenerate's snapshot is the first regenerate's output (one-step undo only).

Out of scope: multi-step undo history (single-step intentionally); UI (US-149); auto-snapshot before manual edits in the lesson editor; rolling back if generation is interrupted between snapshot-write and lesson.json-write (the file ops are sequential — failure between them leaves the snapshot orphaned, which is acceptable: undo is a UX nicety, not a transactional guarantee).
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
stories.notes: Single-step undo via .lesson-prev.json is a deliberate trade-off — multi-step would need a history directory + cleanup policy, which is out of scope for one iteration. The 'snapshot only on regenerate' policy avoids clobbering across different mutation paths.
