acceptanceCriteria: New GET /api/courses/[slug]/export/zip/route.ts: streams an application/zip response (Content-Disposition: `attachment; filename="<slug>-<ISO-date>.zip"`). Uses a streaming zip lib — prefer `archiver` if not already a dependency (lightweight, no native deps); add to package.json. ZIP root contains a single folder `<slug>/` whose contents mirror /courses/<slug>/ EXCEPT for these excluded files (matched by exact basename): `.generation-state.json`, `.generating.json`, `.generation-events.ndjson`, `.generation-events.*.ndjson` (rotated logs), `.lesson-prev.json` files (snapshot artifacts), `coherence-report.md` is INCLUDED if present.

Slug validated via assertSafeSlug. Returns 404 if /courses/<slug>/ missing, 500 on stream errors. Returns 409 if a generation is currently active for that slug (taking a snapshot mid-generation could capture inconsistent state — better to fail loudly).

Add `Export as ZIP` item to the dropdown menu introduced in US-142 (between Extend and Delete or at the end — final placement chosen to keep destructive Delete last). `data-testid="course-menu-export-zip-<slug>"`. Click triggers a download by setting window.location.href to the export URL (browser handles the download stream natively); no client-side blob assembly. Show a brief toast `"Preparing ZIP export…"` immediately on click.

Unit/integration test in src/app/api/courses/[slug]/export/zip/route.test.ts (or via a server-test): with a seeded course on disk including one of each excluded file, hit the route, capture the response stream, parse the ZIP entries, assert exactly which files are included/excluded by name. Verify the response Content-Disposition header.

Verify in browser using playwright-skill: seed a course, open three-dots → click Export as ZIP → assert a download is triggered (Playwright's `page.waitForEvent('download')`). Save to /tmp, unzip, assert structure matches expectations. Reference the test output in the progress report.

Out of scope: progress bar for large courses (rare — most courses are small JSON + small uploads); resumable downloads; encryption/password protection; signed URLs (single-user local app, no auth model); bundling /courses/.trash/ entries (only live courses).
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
Verify in browser using playwright-skill
stories.notes: GET (not POST) is correct here — export is read-only, idempotent, browser-native download. Streaming via archiver avoids holding the whole ZIP in memory for courses with large source uploads.

stories.title: Course ZIP import: greyed drag-drop card as last entry in explorer
stories.description: As a course author, I want a drag-and-drop import card always rendered as the last entry in the home course explorer — visually greyed-out with a dashed border to signal its different role — so I can drag a previously-exported ZIP (US-150) onto it to import the course into this instance.
acceptanceCriteria: In src/app/page.tsx, after the list of real course cards, render a final `ImportCourseCard` component with `data-testid="import-course-card"`. Visual style: same dimensions as a course card; background `var(--bg-muted)` or 50%-opacity; dashed 2px border in `var(--text-tertiary)`; centered icon (lucide `Upload`) + label `Drop course ZIP here` + subtext `or click to browse`. Hover state: dashed border → solid `var(--accent)`, opacity 0.8.

Drag-over state: visual feedback (border becomes solid accent, background becomes accent-soft). DragLeave + Drop reset to default. Drop with non-zip file → toast `"Only .zip files are supported."`, no upload. Drop with zip → POST to /api/courses/import as multipart/form-data with field name `file`. Click on card opens native file picker accepting `.zip` only.

New POST /api/courses/import/route.ts handler: receives multipart, extracts file (max 100MB to keep memory bounded), writes to a temp dir under os.tmpdir(), unzips via `unzipper` or `adm-zip` (add to package.json if missing — prefer streaming `unzipper` for memory). Validates: top-level entry is a single folder named `<slug>` matching /^[a-z0-9-]+$/, that folder contains a course.json which validates against CourseSchema, and any lesson JSONs validate against LessonSchema. If validation passes AND /courses/<slug>/ does NOT already exist, move the extracted folder into /courses/<slug>/ via fs.rename (cross-device fallback). Returns 200 with `{ slug, lessonCount }`. Returns 400 on validation failure (with specific reason: `not-zip`, `bad-structure`, `invalid-course-json`, `invalid-lesson-json`), 409 if the slug already exists locally with `{ existingSlug: <slug> }` (NO auto-rename in this story — user must remove or rename existing course manually first).

On 200: the home explorer refetches the course list and the newly-imported course card slides into place. Toast `"Imported <course title>"`. On 409: toast `"A course with slug \"<slug>\" already exists. Delete or rename it first."`. On 400 with reason: tailored toast (`"Invalid course archive: <reason>"`).

Security: enforce ZIP-slip protection — every entry path inside the ZIP must, after resolution, remain within the temp extraction dir; reject and 400 with `bad-structure` if any entry escapes. Reject ZIPs containing symlinks. Cap total uncompressed size to 500MB to prevent zip-bomb.

Verify in browser using playwright-skill: prepare a valid course ZIP fixture in tests (or generate at test setup by streaming via archiver, mirroring US-150's output). Load /, screenshot showing import card greyed at end of list. Programmatically drop the fixture file via Playwright's setInputFiles on the hidden file input (since real drag-drop is finicky — the click-to-browse path covers the same backend). Screenshot success state with new card. Reference screenshots.

Out of scope: previewing course contents before import (no UI inspect step — accept-or-reject from disk validation only); importing into a different slug than the ZIP's folder name (slug is fixed by ZIP contents); merging into an existing course; importing only specific lessons; signed/encrypted imports.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
Verify in browser using playwright-skill
stories.notes: ZIP-slip protection + size cap are non-negotiable for any unzip endpoint, even in a single-user local app — defense-in-depth. The 'no auto-rename on conflict' policy is intentional: silent renames create confusing dual entries.

stories.title: Course static HTML export with embedded Pyodide (publish-ready)
stories.description: As a course author who wants to publish a course outside the dev-server, I want a static HTML export that produces a self-contained ZIP of pre-rendered .html files (one per lesson + an index.html with module navigation) where code widgets remain functional via embedded Pyodide loaded from a CDN — no Node.js, no Next.js runtime required to view the course locally or host it on any static host.
acceptanceCriteria: New GET /api/courses/[slug]/export/html/route.ts: returns ZIP with structure `<slug>/index.html` (course landing page with module/lesson links), `<slug>/lessons/<lessonSlug>.html` per lesson, `<slug>/assets/styles.css` (inlined design tokens + minimal print/screen CSS extracted from the live app), and `<slug>/assets/pyodide-loader.js` (a small wrapper that loads Pyodide from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/<pinned-version>/full/pyodide.js` and exposes `runPython(code: string): Promise<string>`).

Per-lesson HTML rendering: server-side renders each Lesson via the SAME components used in src/app/courses/[slug]/lessons/[lessonSlug]/page.tsx, but with a STATIC variant that omits these interactive features: AI tutor chat (US-135), per-lesson regenerate UI (US-149), section pencil-panel (US-147), live generation log, progress tracking (no writes to ~/.ai-lecturer). Code widgets (Code, CodeCloze) are kept functional: they use the embedded pyodide-loader.js to run Python in-browser. Quiz widgets are kept functional with answer-checking client-side. Theory + Demo widgets are pure render. Sandbox is rendered read-only.

Implementation approach: introduce src/lib/export/staticRender.ts that uses React's `renderToStaticMarkup` from react-dom/server to produce the per-lesson HTML strings, wrapping with a minimal `<!doctype html>` shell containing `<link rel="stylesheet" href="../assets/styles.css">`, `<script src="../assets/pyodide-loader.js" defer></script>`, and `<script src="<lessonSlug>.data.js" defer></script>` (a tiny per-lesson JS payload containing the lesson JSON + initialization code that mounts the static-React-component-tree onto the page if any client interactivity is needed for code/quiz widgets). The static variant of widget components conditionally skips interactive controls based on a `mode: 'static'` prop.

Pyodide version pinning: a single PYODIDE_VERSION constant in src/lib/export/constants.ts (e.g., `0.27.4`) used across the loader script and any tests. Document in README.md that internet access is required for Pyodide CDN load on first viewing of an exported course (an offline-bundle option is explicitly out of scope).

ZIP excludes anything not needed for static viewing: no .ts/.tsx, no node_modules, no course-spec.json (the spec is implementation detail of the in-app generator, not user-facing), no /sources/ uploads (user can re-upload if importing back via US-151 with a different ZIP — static export is for VIEWING not for re-importing into the dev app).

Slug validated, 404 on missing, 409 on busy, returns ZIP with Content-Disposition `attachment; filename="<slug>-static-<ISO-date>.zip"`. Add `Export as static HTML` item to the course three-dots menu (US-142) — `data-testid="course-menu-export-html-<slug>"`. Click triggers download (window.location.href to URL).

Integration test: seed a course with one theory lesson + one code lesson + one quiz lesson. Hit the route. Unzip in /tmp. Open `<slug>/lessons/theory-lesson.html` via Playwright's `page.goto('file:///tmp/.../theory-lesson.html')` — assert content renders without console errors. Open the code lesson — wait for Pyodide to load (Playwright network: allow CDN), assert `runPython('1+1')` returns '2' via an injected eval. Open the quiz lesson — click the correct option, assert client-side checking marks it green. Reference screenshots.

Out of scope: offline-bundled Pyodide (would balloon ZIP size by ~10MB+); supporting non-Python code widgets (current widgets are all Python-based); serving over HTTPS / hosting recommendations (user's choice); SEO/meta tags optimization (basic <title> only); analytics/tracking; multi-language UI (export uses the active app locale at export time only).
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
Verify in browser using playwright-skill
stories.notes: Static HTML is the user's stretch goal — kept as a separate story so US-150 (ZIP export) and US-151 (ZIP import) can ship independently if this one runs into Pyodide-vs-renderToStaticMarkup compatibility issues. CDN-loaded Pyodide keeps the export ZIP small but requires net access on first viewing.

stories.title: Per-lesson PDF export via puppeteer (clean, no-interactions)
stories.description: As a course author, I want a Print to PDF action on each lesson that produces a clean, printable PDF (theory + Demo + Quiz answers visible, no interactive controls, no nav, no AI tutor) suitable for printing or sharing offline. The PDF is server-rendered via puppeteer/playwright headless from a dedicated /print route.
acceptanceCriteria: New internal route src/app/courses/[slug]/lessons/[lessonSlug]/print/page.tsx: server-rendered minimal layout (no header, no sidebar, no nav, no AI tutor chat, no pencil-panels, no regen buttons). Renders the lesson's sections in order with print-friendly styles (sans-serif body, 12pt baseline, page-break-inside: avoid on widgets, `@media print` rules promoting black-on-white from theme). Quiz sections render with the correct answer visibly highlighted (since this is for printing reference material, not interaction). Code sections render code blocks WITH the hidden tests still hidden by default (preserves the 'code tests hidden' design decision per project memory) but with a distinct `[Tests hidden]` placeholder. Sandbox sections render the prompt only.

New GET /api/courses/[slug]/lessons/[lessonSlug]/export/pdf/route.ts: Uses puppeteer-core + a Chromium binary. Prefer reusing the playwright Chromium already installed via scripts/ralph/skills/playwright-skill (its node_modules contains chromium). The route launches headless Chromium pointing at `http://localhost:<active-port>/courses/<slug>/lessons/<lessonSlug>/print`, awaits networkidle, calls page.pdf({ format: 'A4', margin: { top: '20mm', right: '15mm', bottom: '20mm', left: '15mm' }, printBackground: true }), returns the buffer with `Content-Type: application/pdf` + `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<lessonSlug>.pdf"`. Browser launch is gated behind a server-side singleton (one browser instance reused across export calls, lazily started, idle-timeout-closed after 5min) to avoid spawning Chromium per-request.

Active-port detection: read process.env.PORT or default to 3000; if the print route fetch fails with ECONNREFUSED, return 503 `"Dev server not running — start it before exporting PDF."`. Retries: one retry after 500ms before returning 503.

Add `Print to PDF` button in the lesson page header next to the Regenerate button from US-149 — `data-testid="export-lesson-pdf-btn"`. Click triggers download via window.location.href to the export URL. Toast `"Generating PDF…"` shown immediately, dismissed when the download begins (browser-native download triggers an event we listen for, OR after 30s timeout — whichever first).

Slug + lessonSlug validated. 404 if lesson missing. 409 not relevant (PDF gen is read-only and concurrent-safe — multiple users, hypothetically, could export simultaneously). Errors during page.pdf() return 500 with the error message.

Integration test: seed a lesson with one of each section type (theory + quiz + code + sandbox + demo). Hit the export route via fetch. Save response to /tmp/<lessonSlug>.pdf. Verify the file is a valid PDF by inspecting magic bytes (`%PDF-`). Optionally use `pdf-parse` to extract text and assert the lesson title appears, the quiz question + correct answer appear, and the code block content appears. Reference test output.

Verify in browser using playwright-skill: load a lesson, click Print to PDF, assert a download is triggered (Playwright's page.waitForEvent('download')), save to /tmp, validate PDF magic bytes. Reference screenshots of the lesson view + the generated PDF (rendered as image) in the progress report.

Out of scope: full-course PDF (one lesson at a time per product decision); custom page templates (single A4 layout); custom margins via UI; OCR-friendly PDFs; PDF accessibility tagging (PDF/UA); embedding interactive elements (PDF is print-optimized — no JS execution).
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
Verify in browser using playwright-skill
stories.notes: Reusing the playwright-skill's Chromium avoids adding a separate puppeteer-chromium dependency (~150MB). The browser singleton is critical — naive per-request launches would make exports take 5-10s each due to Chromium startup. The 'tests hidden' detail preserves the project's documented UX decision (project memory: code-widget tests hidden by default).

stories.title: TTS/STT infrastructure: Coqui XTTS + whisper.cpp via subprocess + /api/tts + /api/stt
stories.description: As a developer setting up the platform, I want server-side TTS and STT infrastructure using open-source engines (Coqui XTTS for TTS, whisper.cpp for STT) wrapped behind stable HTTP routes (/api/tts, /api/stt) so that audio widgets (US-155, US-156) and lesson generation (US-157) can call them without coupling to a specific engine. Both engines run locally (no API keys, no cloud calls) via subprocess.
acceptanceCriteria: Setup script scripts/setup-tts.sh: detects platform (Linux/WSL2 for now), installs Coqui XTTS via `pipx install coqui-tts` (or `pip install coqui-tts` into a virtualenv at scripts/.venv/coqui/), downloads the default English voice model on first run (xtts_v2 or equivalent — whichever is current as of model-installation date), and verifies installation by running a 1-second test synthesis. Idempotent (skip steps if already done). Documented in README.md under a new `## Optional: TTS/STT setup` section.

Setup script scripts/setup-stt.sh: clones + builds whisper.cpp into scripts/.bin/whisper.cpp/ (using `make` — requires gcc/clang), downloads the `ggml-base.en.bin` model into scripts/.bin/whisper.cpp/models/. Idempotent. Documented alongside the TTS setup.

New POST /api/tts/route.ts: body Zod-validated `{ text: string (1..2000), voice?: 'en-female' | 'en-male' (default 'en-female'), outputBaseName?: string (defaults to a content-hash) }`. Spawns the TTS CLI (`scripts/.venv/coqui/bin/tts --text "<text>" --model_name tts_models/multilingual/multi-dataset/xtts_v2 --speaker <voice-mapped> --language_idx en --out_path <tmpfile>.wav` or equivalent based on the installed package's actual CLI shape). Captures the .wav file, moves it to `~/.ai-lecturer/tts-cache/<outputBaseName>.wav` (a content-hash filename ensures dedup across calls with identical text+voice), returns `{ audioPath: <relative path under ~/.ai-lecturer/>, durationMs: <computed via ffprobe or wav-header parse>, cached: <true if file already existed> }`.

New POST /api/stt/route.ts: body Zod-validated `{ audioPath: string (must resolve under ~/.ai-lecturer/ or /courses/<slug>/assets/), language?: 'en' (default 'en') }`. Spawns `scripts/.bin/whisper.cpp/main -m scripts/.bin/whisper.cpp/models/ggml-base.en.bin -f <resolved-audioPath> -otxt -of <tmp-output-basename>`. Reads <tmp-output-basename>.txt, returns `{ transcript: string, durationMs: number }`. Path-resolution must use path.resolve + a startsWith check against allowed roots — reject with 400 on traversal attempts.

Both routes detect missing-installation: if the TTS or STT binary/venv is not present, return 503 with `{ error: 'tts-not-installed', message: 'Run scripts/setup-tts.sh first.' }` (or the equivalent for STT). Server startup does NOT require these to be installed — the routes are graceful at request time.

Cache directory ~/.ai-lecturer/tts-cache/ has a soft-cap LRU policy: a small helper in src/lib/server/tts-cache.ts evicts the oldest files when total size exceeds 500MB. Run on every successful TTS call (cheap O(N) scan since N is small).
Add new env var docs to README.md: `AI_LECTURER_TTS_VOICE_FEMALE`, `AI_LECTURER_TTS_VOICE_MALE` for advanced users to override the default speaker IDs (defaults baked into the route).

Unit/integration tests: mock child_process.spawn (using an injectable spawnFactory in src/lib/server/tts.ts and src/lib/server/stt.ts) — verify command shape, verify response shape, verify cache hit/miss behavior, verify path-traversal rejection. NO real Coqui / whisper.cpp invocation in CI (these are heavy + network/install-dependent). The setup scripts are tested manually only and documented as such.

Out of scope: non-English languages (en only in this story; multilingual XTTS support is configurable later but UI/widget contracts target en); GPU acceleration (CPU only); streaming TTS (full file at a time); voice cloning from user samples; phoneme-level alignment for cloze positioning (US-156 will need word-level timestamps from whisper.cpp's `--print-progress` or `-ot` JSON output — surfaced in /api/stt's response as an optional `segments?: Array<{ start: number, end: number, text: string }>` field; mark this as a stretch addition if time allows in this story, otherwise add in US-156).
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
stories.notes: Subprocess wrapping isolates engine choice from consumers — swapping Coqui for Piper later means changing the route internals only. CPU-only is intentional for portability across user machines. The cache + content-hash naming makes generation re-runs cheap (US-157 will benefit).

stories.title: AudioPlayer widget: schema + component + editor
stories.description: As a course author teaching language or audio-centric content, I want an AudioPlayer widget that plays a referenced audio file with custom controls (play/pause, seek bar, volume, playback speed) and an optional transcript display. This is the simpler of the two audio widgets — pure playback, no exercises.
acceptanceCriteria: Extend src/lib/schemas/lesson.ts with a new `AudioPlayerSection` schema: `{ id: string, kind: 'audio-player', audioPath: string (relative path under /courses/<slug>/assets/audio/), transcript?: string, autoplay?: boolean (default false), title?: string }`. Add to the SectionSchema discriminated union. Add tests in src/lib/schemas/schemas.test.ts covering the new section type (valid + missing audioPath + invalid kind drift).

New widget directory src/widgets/AudioPlayer/ with: AudioPlayerWidget.tsx (player UI), AudioPlayerEditor.tsx (course editor side), schemas.ts (re-export), Widget.test.ts. The player UI uses a native <audio> element with `controls={false}` and custom controls built with shadcn Button/Slider: Play/Pause toggle, current time / total time display, seek slider, volume slider (with mute toggle), playback speed dropdown (0.75x / 1x / 1.25x / 1.5x / 2x). Keyboard: Space toggles play, ArrowLeft/Right seek -5s/+5s. ARIA labels on all controls.

Transcript display: if `transcript` is set, render it below the player in a collapsible <details> element labeled `Show transcript` (closed by default to keep listening-focused). Use the existing prose typography (var(--font-prose)).

Register the widget in src/widgets/registry.ts mapping kind 'audio-player' to AudioPlayerWidget. Verify the lesson page (src/app/courses/[slug]/lessons/[lessonSlug]/page.tsx) renders it via the registry without changes (registry-driven dispatch is already in place).

Editor (course-edit side): AudioPlayerEditor.tsx provides a file-path input (validated to exist under the course's assets/audio/ dir on save — server-side validation in the section update route), an autoplay toggle, an optional title input, and a transcript textarea. NO file upload UI in this story (uploading is handled by the existing course-spec sources flow OR by US-157's TTS-driven generation; manual placement of files in /courses/<slug>/assets/audio/ also works for power users).

Server-side static file serving: lesson pages already serve /courses/<slug>/* via Next.js's existing route handler (or add a passthrough at /api/courses/<slug>/assets/audio/[file] if direct fs serving isn't already wired). Verify mp3, wav, and ogg are served with correct Content-Type and Range support (for seeking). If not already wired, add the route handler with content-type detection (mime-types lib already in dependencies, fall back to mime sniff if not present — DO NOT add a new dep just for this).

Verify in browser using playwright-skill: seed a lesson with one AudioPlayer section pointing to a small <500KB .wav fixture file pre-placed at /courses/<slug>/assets/audio/test.wav. Load the lesson, screenshot the player. Click Play, wait 1s, assert audio.currentTime > 0. Click the speed dropdown, select 2x, assert playbackRate=2. Open the transcript <details>, screenshot transcript visible. Reference all screenshots.

Out of scope: waveform visualization; chapters/markers; multi-track audio; speed-changes-pitch-preserved (browser default behavior); subtitle/caption support beyond plain transcript; offline caching beyond browser default; download button (not all uploads should be downloadable — controlled by lesson author's choice elsewhere).
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
Verify in browser using playwright-skill
stories.notes: AudioPlayer is the simpler 'just plays audio' widget — separate from the cloze-exercise widget (US-156) so the player implementation stays focused. Reuses the existing /courses static file serving path; if that path is not already wired for audio MIME types, US-155 adds it.

stories.title: Transcript-cloze widget: listen + fill missing words exercise
stories.description: As a language learner, I want a transcript-cloze widget that plays an audio clip and shows its transcript with selected words replaced by input blanks I must fill in by listening — with per-blank correct/incorrect feedback on submit. The author chooses which words become blanks at edit time.
acceptanceCriteria: Extend src/lib/schemas/lesson.ts with `TranscriptClozeSection`: `{ id: string, kind: 'transcript-cloze', audioPath: string, transcript: string, blanks: Array<{ wordIndex: number, answer: string, hint?: string }>, title?: string, instructions?: string }`. wordIndex is the 0-based position in the whitespace-tokenized transcript. answer is the expected token (case-insensitive matching by default; punctuation stripped before compare). Schema validation: each wordIndex must be in [0, transcriptWordCount), no duplicates. Add to SectionSchema union + tests.

New widget directory src/widgets/TranscriptCloze/: TranscriptClozeWidget.tsx, TranscriptClozeEditor.tsx, Widget.test.ts. The student-facing component renders an AudioPlayer (reuse the component from US-155 by importing it) at top + the transcript below with each blank rendered as an <input> with width matching the answer's character length (style: --w in ch units). After all blanks filled and `Submit` clicked: each input is colored green if correct (case-insensitive, punctuation-stripped match) or red with the correct answer shown beneath in muted text. Score `<X>/<N> correct` displayed at bottom. A `Try again` button resets all inputs.

Editor: TranscriptClozeEditor.tsx provides a transcript textarea + a click-to-toggle-blank UI: each whitespace-tokenized word becomes a clickable chip; clicking toggles whether it's a blank. Selected (blank) words are highlighted in accent. The blanks array is recomputed on every toggle. Hint can be set per-blank in a small inline field that appears when the chip is selected. The editor saves the section schema unchanged to lesson.json via the existing lesson-update route.

Tokenization helper in src/lib/widgets/transcriptTokenize.ts: `tokenize(transcript: string): Array<{ index: number, text: string, isPunctuation: boolean }>`. Whitespace-split, strip-and-track trailing punctuation. Tested for common cases (English with punctuation, contractions like "don't" treated as one token). Used by both the renderer (to map blanks to their positions) and the editor (to render clickable chips).

Progress integration: the widget reports its score via the existing per-section progress mechanism (see src/lib/schemas/progress.ts — extend the SectionStateSchema if needed to include `score?: { correct: number, total: number }` for this widget; if SectionStateSchema is already flexible, no schema change). Persists to ~/.ai-lecturer/progress.json via the existing progress write path.

Verify in browser using playwright-skill: seed a lesson with one TranscriptCloze section: transcript `"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"`, blanks `[{wordIndex:1,answer:'quick'},{wordIndex:5,answer:'over'}]`, audioPath pointing to a small fixture .wav. Load the lesson, screenshot showing two input blanks. Type 'quick' + 'over', click Submit, screenshot showing both green + score 2/2. Reload, type 'fast' + 'over', Submit, screenshot showing first red with correct answer shown, second green, score 1/2. Reference screenshots.

Out of scope: typo-tolerant matching (Levenshtein distance — strict match for now); multi-blank words (each blank is exactly one token); audio segment playback per-blank (full audio only — 'play just this word' is a stretch goal for a future story leveraging US-154's segments output); generating cloze positions automatically from audio difficulty heuristics (manual selection only).
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
Verify in browser using playwright-skill
stories.notes: Builds on US-155 (AudioPlayer reused as a sub-component). Strict matching keeps the first version simple — typo tolerance can be added later without breaking the schema. The author-side toggle-by-clicking UI matches common cloze-editor patterns and avoids a separate 'enter blanks JSON' UX.

stories.title: Generation integration: TTS for AudioPlayer + transcript-cloze sections during lesson gen
stories.description: As a course author generating a language-focused course, I want the lesson generation pipeline to automatically synthesize audio via TTS (US-154) for any AudioPlayer or transcript-cloze section the agent emits, so the audio file is in /courses/<slug>/assets/audio/ before the lesson is marked done — without me manually uploading audio for every clip.
acceptanceCriteria: Update scripts/ralph/skills/generate_lesson/generate_lesson.md (and any companion .md files for the generate_lesson skill): document that for AudioPlayer and transcript-cloze sections the agent should emit `audioPath: 'AUTO_TTS'` (a sentinel value) and provide a `audioSourceText` field on the section temporarily — this field is consumed by the post-processor and stripped before final write. The `transcript` field for transcript-cloze sections IS the audio source (no separate audioSourceText needed for cloze); for AudioPlayer the audioSourceText is the spoken content.

src/lib/server/generation.ts post-processing step: after the per-lesson generate_lesson spawn completes and the JSON parses + validates against an EXTENDED LessonSchema that allows the AUTO_TTS sentinel, scan the parsed Lesson for sections with `audioPath === 'AUTO_TTS'`. For each such section, derive the source text (transcript for transcript-cloze; audioSourceText for AudioPlayer), call POST /api/tts internally (or call the underlying TTS function directly to avoid HTTP overhead — extract a callable from US-154's route into src/lib/server/tts.ts), get back the cached/new audio file path, copy/move the audio into /courses/<slug>/assets/audio/<lessonSlug>-<sectionId>.wav, replace audioPath with the relative path `assets/audio/<lessonSlug>-<sectionId>.wav`, strip audioSourceText from the section. Write the final lesson.json after all TTS calls complete.

Failure handling: if any TTS call fails (engine missing, text too long, etc.), mark the lesson generation as failed for that lesson — emit `stage:failed` with the TTS error in the message, do NOT write a partial lesson.json with AUTO_TTS placeholders (avoid corrupted state). The user's recourse is to install TTS (US-154 setup) or to manually edit the generated section to remove the audio component. The .tmp partial lesson is cleaned up.

Pipeline event integration: emit a sub-stage event `stage:tts` for each audio section with payload `{ lessonSlug, sectionId, status: 'started'|'done'|'failed' }` so the live generation log (existing US-128 / US-130 SSE) shows TTS progress. These events sit between the lesson's generate_lesson `stage:done` and the lesson's overall completion event.

stories.title: TTS (Coqui XTTS) auto-uses CUDA when available, falls back to CPU
stories.description: As a power user with an NVIDIA GPU, I want the TTS subprocess to detect CUDA availability at startup and run inference on the GPU for substantially faster synthesis. On systems without CUDA (most laptops, CI), behavior is unchanged — CPU inference as today.
acceptanceCriteria: A failing test reproducing the lack of GPU detection exists before the change: a unit test in src/lib/server/tts.test.ts asserts that when a mocked CUDA probe returns `available=true`, the spawned `tts` command line includes `--use_cuda true`; the test should fail against current main (which never passes the flag).

Add a one-shot CUDA probe helper in src/lib/server/tts.ts (or a new src/lib/server/gpu.ts shared with STT in US-168): `async function isCudaAvailable(): Promise<boolean>`. Implementation: spawn `python3 -c 'import torch; print(int(torch.cuda.is_available()))'` against the same venv that hosts the Coqui binary (derived from `coquiBinPath()` — sibling `python3` in `scripts/.venv/coqui/bin/`). Result is memoized for the process lifetime (the answer doesn't change without a restart). On any error (non-zero exit, no torch, ENOENT), return false silently — never throw — and log once at info level `TTS CUDA probe failed, using CPU: <reason>`.

When `isCudaAvailable()` returns true, the spawned `tts` command in src/lib/server/tts.ts adds `--use_cuda true` to its argv. When false, argv is unchanged from current behavior (CPU inference, identical to today). The probe runs once on the first /api/tts request and the result is cached.

Env override: `AI_LECTURER_TTS_DEVICE` accepts `cuda`, `cpu`, or `auto` (default). `cuda` forces the flag without probing (errors propagate if the GPU isn't actually present); `cpu` skips the probe and forces CPU; `auto` is the probe behavior above. Document this in the TtsNotInstalledError vicinity (top of file comments).

Unit tests in src/lib/server/tts.test.ts: (1) probe-true path → argv contains `--use_cuda true`; (2) probe-false path → argv does NOT contain `--use_cuda`; (3) AI_LECTURER_TTS_DEVICE=cuda forces the flag without probing; (4) AI_LECTURER_TTS_DEVICE=cpu skips the flag even if probe would succeed; (5) probe error returns false and does not throw. Mock the spawn function via the existing test pattern for spawn injection.

No change to /api/tts request/response contract; no change to TtsRequest/TtsResponse schemas; no change to tts-cache (cache keys stay text+voice only — cuda vs cpu produces equivalent audio for cache purposes, and we don't want device toggling to invalidate the cache).
Out of scope: STT/whisper.cpp GPU support (separate story US-168); a UI toggle for the device (env var only for now); reporting which device was used in the API response; multi-GPU selection.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
stories.notes: TTS spawn site: src/lib/server/tts.ts. Coqui XTTS supports `--use_cuda true`. Probe via the venv python that owns Coqui.

stories.title: STT (whisper.cpp) auto-uses CUDA when available, falls back to CPU
stories.description: As a power user with an NVIDIA GPU, I want whisper.cpp to use the CUDA-built `whisper-cli` when one is detected, for faster transcription. On systems without CUDA, behavior is unchanged — the existing CPU `whisper-cli` is used as today.
acceptanceCriteria: A failing test reproducing the lack of GPU detection exists before the change: a unit test in src/lib/server/stt.test.ts asserts that when a mocked CUDA-binary probe returns `available=true`, the spawn invocation uses the CUDA-enabled binary path AND, where applicable, includes whisper.cpp's GPU flag (e.g. omits `--no-gpu` and/or sets `-gpu` per the local whisper.cpp build's CLI). Test should fail against current main.

Add a STT-specific probe in src/lib/server/stt.ts (or reuse src/lib/server/gpu.ts shared with US-167): `async function whisperCudaAvailable(): Promise<{ available: boolean, binaryPath: string }>`. Probe order: (1) check for a CUDA-built whisper-cli at `scripts/.whisper-cuda/build/bin/whisper-cli` (or env override `AI_LECTURER_WHISPER_CUDA_BIN`); (2) if present and `nvidia-smi` exits 0, return `{available:true, binaryPath:<cuda-path>}`; (3) otherwise return `{available:false, binaryPath:<existing CPU path>}`. Memoize for process lifetime. Any probe error → return CPU path, log once `STT CUDA probe failed, using CPU: <reason>`.

When the probe returns `available=true`, the spawn in src/lib/server/stt.ts uses the CUDA binary path. CPU path is the existing default — argv unchanged from today. If whisper.cpp's CUDA binary needs additional flags (e.g. `-ngl <n>` for GPU layers), include them; if it auto-uses GPU when available, no extra flag is needed — verify against the locally installed binary's `--help` output and document the chosen invocation in a comment.

Env override: `AI_LECTURER_STT_DEVICE` accepts `cuda`, `cpu`, `auto` (default). `cuda` forces the CUDA binary (errors propagate if missing); `cpu` forces the existing CPU binary; `auto` is the probe behavior. Document near SttNotInstalledError.

Setup: extend scripts/setup-stt.sh (or add scripts/setup-stt-cuda.sh as a peer) so the user can opt-in to building the CUDA whisper.cpp binary. The script must NOT run automatically during normal setup — CUDA build requires the CUDA toolkit. Document the opt-in flag in the script's header comments.

Unit tests in src/lib/server/stt.test.ts: (1) probe-true path → spawn uses CUDA binary path; (2) probe-false path → spawn uses existing CPU binary; (3) AI_LECTURER_STT_DEVICE=cuda forces CUDA path even if probe wouldn't pick it; (4) AI_LECTURER_STT_DEVICE=cpu skips CUDA even if available; (5) missing CUDA binary returns CPU and does not throw. Mock spawn + filesystem stat via existing test patterns.
No change to /api/stt request/response contract; no change to SttRequest/SttResponse schemas; transcode-to-WAV step (existing) is unchanged.

Out of scope: TTS GPU support (separate story US-167); auto-building the CUDA binary as part of normal setup; UI toggle (env var only); reporting device in the API response; selecting which GPU layer count (-ngl) to use beyond a single sensible default.

stories.title: cv2 shim in Pyodide worker — let `import cv2` work in the browser via scipy.ndimage + scikit-image
stories.description: As a course author, I want lessons that import cv2 to actually execute in browser-side Pyodide so learners can run and edit real OpenCV-looking code instead of seeing snippets marked `# illustrative — the lesson player does not execute it`. Pyodide has no native OpenCV port, so we ship a thin Python shim that re-exposes the OpenCV API subset used by lessons on top of scipy.ndimage + scikit-image (both already loadable in Pyodide).
acceptanceCriteria: New file `scripts/pyodide/cv2_shim.py` exists and implements the following OpenCV API subset as wrappers over scipy.ndimage + skimage.feature + skimage.io + skimage.color: constants `IMREAD_GRAYSCALE = 0`, `IMREAD_COLOR = 1`, `CV_8U = 0`, `CV_64F = 6`; functions `imread(path, flags=IMREAD_COLOR)` (uses `skimage.io.imread`, converts to grayscale via `skimage.color.rgb2gray` when flag is GRAYSCALE; returns uint8 in grayscale path), `imwrite(path, img)` (uses `skimage.io.imsave`, returns True), `Sobel(src, ddepth, dx, dy, ksize=3)` (uses `scipy.ndimage.sobel(src.astype(np.float64), axis=1)` for dx=1/dy=0 and `axis=0` for dx=0/dy=1; raises ValueError for other combinations; ksize argument accepted but only 3×3 supported), `Canny(image, threshold1, threshold2)` (uses `skimage.feature.canny(img.astype(np.float64)/255.0, low_threshold=threshold1/255.0, high_threshold=threshold2/255.0)`, returns uint8 mask with values {0, 255}).
Module ends with `sys.modules['cv2'] = sys.modules[__name__]` so `import cv2` in user code resolves to the shim.

Top-of-file docstring explicitly documents: (a) this is a shim, not real OpenCV; (b) numerically NOT 1:1 with OpenCV — different default Gaussian sigma in Canny, different sobel kernel scaling — visual results similar but pixel-exact comparisons will differ; (c) only a subset of cv2 API is implemented (the functions listed above), adding new functions requires extending this file; (d) Sobel `ksize` only supports 3 (scipy.ndimage.sobel is fixed at 3×3); (e) consumers must call this through the Pyodide worker — see `src/lib/pyodide/CLAUDE.md`.

`src/widgets/Code/schema.ts` `CodeDataSchema` is extended with optional `requiresPackages?: string[]` field (zod: `z.array(z.string()).optional()`). When set, the worker will load those packages before executing the user's code. The current canonical value is `['cv2']`.

`src/lib/pyodide/worker.ts` gains `ensureCv2Shim(py)` modeled on existing `ensurePexp` / `ensureGauss` (worker.ts:143-195): module-level boolean `cv2InstalledOnce = false`; function awaits `py.loadPackage(['scipy', 'scikit-image'])` then `py.runPythonAsync(CV2_SHIM_PY)` then sets `cv2InstalledOnce = true`; subsequent calls are no-ops. `CV2_SHIM_PY` is a string constant containing the contents of `scripts/pyodide/cv2_shim.py` (read at build/bundle time — match how PEXP_PY is currently inlined in worker.ts).

`RunRequest` types in worker.ts (the `run` and `runWithTests` payload variants around worker.ts:221) are extended with optional `requiresPackages?: string[]`. Before exec'ing user code in those handlers, if the array contains `'cv2'`, await `ensureCv2Shim(py)`. Same plumbing for `client.ts`: the public `run` and `runWithTests` APIs accept an optional `requiresPackages?: string[]` and forward it in the postMessage payload.

Unit test in `src/lib/pyodide/runner.test.ts`: a test named `cv2 shim — Sobel returns same-shape float array` runs `import cv2; import numpy as np; img = np.zeros((8, 8), dtype=np.uint8); img[2:6, 2:6] = 255; gx = cv2.Sobel(img, cv2.CV_64F, 1, 0); assert gx.shape == (8, 8); assert gx.dtype == np.float64` through the worker with `requiresPackages: ['cv2']` — expect no traceback and assert no error in result.

Unit test in same file: a test named `cv2 shim — Canny returns binary uint8` runs `import cv2; import numpy as np; img = np.zeros((32, 32), dtype=np.uint8); img[8:24, 8:24] = 255; edges = cv2.Canny(img, 100, 200); assert edges.dtype == np.uint8; assert set(int(v) for v in np.unique(edges).tolist()) <= {0, 255}; assert edges.max() == 255` through the worker. Expect no traceback.

Discoverability for future agents (USER REQUIREMENT): new file `src/lib/pyodide/CLAUDE.md` documents the cv2 shim. It must include: a 1-paragraph summary stating that `cv2` in Pyodide is a shim built on scipy + skimage, not the real OpenCV; a list of currently-implemented functions and constants; the known divergences from real OpenCV (Canny sigma, Sobel scaling, ksize=3 only); how to extend the shim (add function to `scripts/pyodide/cv2_shim.py`, no worker changes needed since the shim is loaded as a Python module); pointer to `scripts/pyodide/cv2_shim.py`. ALSO: append a single bullet to the `## Codebase Patterns` section at the top of `scripts/ralph/progress.txt` reading something like `- cv2 in Pyodide is a shim over scipy.ndimage + skimage (scripts/pyodide/cv2_shim.py) — NOT real OpenCV; subset of API; see src/lib/pyodide/CLAUDE.md`. ALSO: add a one-line JSDoc-style comment above the `requiresPackages` field in `src/widgets/Code/schema.ts` reading `// 'cv2' resolves to a shim, not real OpenCV — see src/lib/pyodide/CLAUDE.md`.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
stories.notes: Foundation for US-174 (live output) and US-175 (edge-detection lesson rewrite). Pyodide does not ship OpenCV (no WASM port exists as an official wheel); scipy + scikit-image cover ~80% of the OpenCV image-processing surface used by lessons, so we wrap them in a `cv2`-shaped facade. Numeric divergence is acceptable for pedagogy — lessons should not assert pixel-exact equality with real-OpenCV output. The shim is `lazy-loaded` (~5MB of skimage on first use) so non-cv2 lessons stay fast. Discoverability AC was added per user request so future agents extending image-processing lessons don't assume real OpenCV semantics.

stories.title: LessonChat: STT mic button with hybrid Web Speech / `/api/stt/upload` fallback, transcript fills the chat input
stories.description: As a learner chatting with the AI tutor, I want a microphone button next to the chat input so I can dictate my question instead of typing. First click starts capture, second click ends it; the transcribed text is appended to the textarea so I can review/edit it before sending.
acceptanceCriteria: src/components/LessonChat.tsx: render an icon button immediately to the LEFT of the existing textarea (or inside the same input row, before any send button). Icon: Lucide `Mic` when idle, `Square` (stop) when capturing. data-testid: `lesson-chat-stt-toggle`. aria-label cycles between `Start voice input` and `Stop voice input`. Button is enabled whenever the textarea would be enabled (i.e. not while a reply is mid-stream — disable during streaming).

Hybrid capture strategy in a new helper `src/lib/client/sttCapture.ts` (or inline if it stays under ~120 lines): on toggle-start, check `typeof window !== 'undefined' && (window.SpeechRecognition || window.webkitSpeechRecognition)`. If present, create an instance with `continuous = true`, `interimResults = true`, `lang` derived from `navigator.language` (fall back to `'en-US'`), and start it. On `onresult`, accumulate `event.results[i][0].transcript` for `isFinal === true` entries into a local buffer; ignore interim results (do not flicker the textarea). On toggle-stop or `onend`, append the final buffer to the existing textarea value (with a single leading space if textarea is non-empty and doesn't end in whitespace) and clear local state.

Fallback path: if `SpeechRecognition` is undefined, OR if it fires `onerror` with `not-allowed`/`service-not-allowed`/`network`, switch to MediaRecorder identical in shape to src/widgets/SttDemo/SttDemoWidget.tsx: `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({ audio: true })`, pick a supported mimeType, record until second click, build a `FormData` with the blob under field name `audio`, POST to `/api/stt/upload`, await JSON `{ text }`, then append `text` to textarea same as the Web Speech path. Chip auto-clears after 5s or when the user clicks the mic again. Existing draft text is NEVER overwritten or lost on error.

Cleanup: stopping capture must call `recognition.stop()` (Web Speech) AND release any MediaRecorder stream tracks (`stream.getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop())`). Unmounting LessonChat while recording must also tear down.

Click the mic button, assert the recording dot appears, click again, assert textarea value equals `unit test transcript`. Then in a second test, delete the SpeechRecognition stub before navigation, mock `/api/stt/upload` via `page.route()` to return `{ text: 'fallback' }`, stub `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia` to return a MediaStream from a generated silent audio track (use `OfflineAudioContext` or `MediaStreamTrackGenerator` — fall back to skipping the assertion if neither works in the headless target and document the skip in the test file comment), click the mic, click again, assert `fallback` lands in textarea.

stories.title: Themed scrollbars across the app (light/dark/sunset) replacing default browser chrome

Sanity smoke test in Vitest (or a CSS unit test if the harness supports it): render a component with `

stories.title: Theory widget: footer `Read ▶` TTS button with cross-widget FIFO generation queue
stories.description: As a learner reading a Theory section, I want a Read button at the bottom of the widget so I can listen to the content. If I trigger Read on a second Theory widget while the first is still generating, the second should queue up and play when the first finishes — never two concurrent generations.
acceptanceCriteria: src/widgets/Theory/TheoryWidget.tsx: render a footer row BELOW the markdown body (inside the existing `data-theory-body` container or as a sibling — pick whichever keeps the outer card layout consistent with the Code widget's submit footer). The footer is left-aligned (mirror of the Code widget's right-aligned submit). Footer contains a single primary-styled button. States: `Read ▶` (idle), `Queued (n)` where n is its 1-based queue position when waiting, `Generating…` with a spinner when in-flight, `▶ Replay` (or just a play icon + `<audio>`) when ready. data-testid: `theory-tts-button`; aria-label reflects current state.

On press while idle: enqueue a job `{ id: uuid, text, voice, status: 'queued' }` into a shared module-level queue at `src/lib/client/ttsQueue.ts`. The queue exports `enqueue(text, voice): { id, subscribe(listener) }` and processes one item at a time via an async worker: pop head → POST to `/api/tts` with `{ text, voice }` → receive audio blob → emit `{ status: 'ready', blobUrl }` → next item. The TheoryWidget subscribes to its own job id and re-renders status accordingly.

Text passed to TTS: derive from `data.markdown` via a `stripForTts(markdown: string): string` helper (new in `src/lib/client/ttsText.ts`) that removes fenced code blocks (```...```), inline code spans, image markdown `![...](...)`, and explicit math delimiters (`$$...$$`, `\[...\]`, `\(...\)`, `$...$`) replacing math with a single space so prose stays grammatical. Strip leftover markdown syntax (headers `#`, bold `**`, italic `_`, link `[text](url)` → keep `text`) using a minimal regex pass — do NOT pull in a full markdown-to-text dep.

Voice: read once via `readTtsVoice()` from `src/lib/client/ttsVoice.ts` at enqueue time (locks the voice for that job). Voice change between jobs is honored — the queue is not flushed on voice change but each enqueue captures the then-current voice.

Cache: keyed by `(text, voice)` → `{ blobUrl, audio?: HTMLAudioElement }` in module-level Map. Subsequent presses on the same widget (text unchanged) with the same voice skip the network and re-render `▶ Replay` immediately. Different voice → re-fetch. Editing the Theory data (different `data.markdown`) invalidates by cache-miss naturally.

Player: once `status === 'ready'`, render an inline `<audio controls src={blobUrl}>` below the button (data-testid `theory-tts-audio`) and auto-play once. Subsequent presses pause/resume the existing element.

Error path: `/api/tts` non-2xx OR network error → emit `{ status: 'error', message }` → button reverts to `Read ▶` with a small inline error chip below (data-testid `theory-tts-error`) reading the server message, auto-clearing after 6s. Errored job does NOT enter the cache. Queue advances to the next item.

Vitest unit test for ttsQueue: with `vi.useFakeTimers()` and a mocked fetch that resolves after 100ms with a deterministic Blob, call `enqueue` three times in immediate succession with different texts. Drive timers forward in 100ms steps. Assert order of completion equals order of enqueue and at no point are two fetches in-flight (track via a counter that fetch mock increments on entry and decrements on resolve — assert max value === 1).

Vitest test for TheoryWidget: mock the ttsQueue module to expose a controllable promise per job. Render two TheoryWidget instances. Click both Read buttons quickly. Assert button 2 shows `Queued (1)` while button 1 shows `Generating…`. Resolve job 1 → button 1 shows `▶ Replay`, button 2 shows `Generating…`. Resolve job 2 → button 2 shows `▶ Replay`.

Vitest test for stripForTts: input markdown containing a fenced ```python block, inline `code`, an image `![alt](src)`, a header `# Heading`, a link `[claude](https://x)`, and inline math `$x^2$` → output is the same text with code/image/math removed, header marker gone, link rendered as `claude`. Snapshot the result.

Verify in browser using playwright-skill: render a lesson with two Theory widgets seeded with distinct prose. Use `page.route('/api/tts')` to delay each response by 800ms and return a small valid MP3 fixture (silent.mp3 under scripts/ralph/skills/playwright-skill/fixtures/, generate if absent — a 200-byte stub will do; if mp3 generation in the test is hard, return a valid WAV with the appropriate Content-Type and confirm the audio element accepts it). Click Read on widget A, then within 100ms click Read on widget B. Assert: at most ONE `/api/tts` request is in-flight at any time (track via `page.on('request')` and `page.on('requestfinished')`); widget B's button shows `Queued (1)` during widget A's generation; both audio elements eventually render; the network log shows two sequential requests, not parallel.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
Verify in browser using playwright-skill
stories.notes: Reuses /api/tts and readTtsVoice (same as US-183 chat speak button). The queue is a module-level singleton — DO NOT use React context; React state across unrelated widget trees would force prop drilling. Out of scope: persisting cached blobs across page reloads (cache is in-memory only — revoke blob URLs on `beforeunload`); a global 'pause all' button; download-as-mp3; per-section TTS (one button reads the whole widget's markdown body); concurrent generation with N>1 workers. The button matches the Code widget's submit-footer visual weight but mirrored to the left edge.
